5. Documents are checked before inspection starts. Staff verify the return note, original order and delivery documents, and reason for return. Mismatches in product, quantity or batch stop the line until resolved with the shift supervisor and stock control. Nothing moves past the inspection benches until paperwork is resolved.

6. Segregation is maintained through the whole inspection. General ambient returns, chilled lines for the +2 °C to +8 °C regime, and hazardous lines for the ventilated 60 m2 hazmat cage are kept apart at all times. Chilled returns are prioritised to protect the cold chain, and hazmat returns go only to the cage and are never mixed with general stock.

7. Every check is scan-recorded with the handheld WMS scanners. Staff scan the return reference, product, batch and location, record accepted and rejected quantities line by line, and label each pallet and carton with inspection status. Unlabelled or unbooked returns never leave Zone F.

8. Damaged, leaking, contaminated or suspect units found during inspection are treated as damaged goods under PR-09. They are labelled, segregated and moved to quarantine within Zone F on the same day they are found, with product, batch, delivery reference and photographs where required, and notified to the shift supervisor and stock control.

9. Inspection ends with a proposal, not a decision. For each inspected line, returns and packing staff propose restock, rework or scrap based on condition, date, packaging and system need. Final disposition belongs only to the shift supervisor, and no return re-enters Zone B or Zone E, goes to rework, or is scrapped without that approval.

10. The inspection area is cleared by record before handover. All counts, inspection results, quarantine transfers and proposals are entered in the system and the shift record, open lines and over-window holds are carried into the end-of-shift handover under PR-15, and all work observes high-visibility vests and class S3 footwear, 10 km/h inside the hall and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and ramps.

title: Disposition Decisions
text:
1. No inspected return leaves Zone F without a disposition decision. Every line inspected under PR-07 is decided as restock, rework or scrap, and no pallet or carton re-enters Zone B or Zone E, moves to value-added packing, or is scrapped without that decision recorded in the system.

2. Returns and packing staff propose, the shift supervisor disposes. For each inspected line staff enter a proposal of restock, rework or scrap with condition, date, packaging and reason evidence on the handheld WMS scanners. The final disposition is approved only by the shift supervisor in charge of the floor, who confirms the inspection before signing.

3. Restock is approved only for fully saleable returns. The supervisor approves restock where every unit has passed inspection, product, batch and expiry match system need, packaging, seal and labelling are intact, and, for chilled lines, the +2 °C to +8 °C regime has been maintained. Anything short of this is not restocked.

4. Restocked goods return only to their directed location. General ambient lines go to bulk storage in Zone B, chilled lines go to Zone E, and hazardous lines go only to the ventilated 60 m2 hazmat cage within its 4,000 kg limit. Each pallet is relabelled, scan-confirmed, and booked as available stock before it leaves Zone F.

5. Rework is approved where the goods are sound but the pack is not. The supervisor approves rework for intact product in damaged outer cartons, mislabelled or display packs, and value-added kitting required by instruction. Rework takes place only in Zone F to instruction by returns and packing staff and re-enters the standard flow for scan-verification and labelling.

6. Scrap is approved where goods cannot be sold or reworked. The supervisor approves scrap for damaged, leaking, contaminated, expired or temperature-failed units, for hazmat lines that cannot be made safe, and for any line where inspection shows loss of identity or integrity. Scrapped lines are segregated as damaged goods under PR-09.

7. Segregation is maintained through the decision. Ambient, chilled and hazmat returns are kept apart in Zone F until moved, chilled stock is returned promptly to Zone E without standing in ambient aisles, and incompatible hazmat classes are never combined. No unbooked, unlabelled or quarantined pallet is placed in racking, pick faces or Zone D.

8. Damaged or suspect lines go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found. The affected units are labelled, segregated and scan-recorded with product, batch, return reference and photographs where required, and notified to the shift supervisor and stock control. No damaged line is restocked, reworked or counted as available stock.

9. Value and system control apply to every decision. No inventory adjustment is ever posted without a second count, proposals by stock controllers require approval before booking, and write-off values follow the fixed split: the shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 500 EUR, and any write-off above 500 EUR is reserved to the warehouse manager.

10. Every proposal, approval, movement and exception is scan-recorded before handover. Product, batch, quantities for restock, rework and scrap, checker and approver names, locations and quarantine references are entered in the system and shift record, and open rework and pending approvals are carried into the end-of-shift handover under PR-15. All work observes high-visibility vests and class S3 footwear, 10 km/h inside the hall and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and ramps.

title: Quarantine and Write-offs
text:
1. All damaged goods are held in quarantine in Zone F from the day they are found under PR-09. Any pallet, carton or unit found damaged, leaking, contaminated, unstable, overweight, mislabelled, expired or temperature-failed in Zone A, Zone B, Zone C, Zone D, Zone E or during returns inspection is moved to the marked quarantine area the same day.

2. Quarantine sits inside the 600 m2 Zone F services and control area, separate from returns inspection, value-added packing and saleable stock. Quarantined ambient, chilled and hazardous lines are kept apart at all times. Hazardous quarantine stays inside the ventilated 60 m2 hazmat cage within its 4,000 kg limit and is never mixed with general quarantine.

3. Every quarantine transfer is labelled and scan-recorded at once. Staff label the affected pallet or carton with product, quantity, batch, location found, damage type, date and finder name, segregate it from correct stock, and scan it with the handheld WMS scanners as quarantine, not as available stock. Photographs are taken where required.

4. Stock control and the shift supervisor are notified of every quarantine. Returns and packing staff or inbound operators record the delivery, order or count reference, stock controllers check the system quantity and hold the location open, and the shift supervisor in charge of the floor secures the goods and directs any making-safe, cleaning or maintenance call.

5. No quarantined goods are restocked, reworked, returned to sale, picked, replenished or dispatched without approval. Quarantine stock is blocked in the system and physically separated. Any bay, face or lane the damage came from stays open only for correct stock until a recount and decision are complete.

6. No inventory adjustment for damaged goods is ever posted without a second count. A different checker recounts the quantity blind, condition is rechecked, and only two matching counts with investigation notes allow a write-off proposal to be prepared by stock control. Damaged quantities are never adjusted away as shrinkage.

7. Write-off approvals follow the fixed value split. The shift supervisor on duty approves damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 500 EUR once quarantine and inspection evidence are complete. Any write-off above 500 EUR is reserved to the warehouse manager and is not posted without the manager's signature.

8. Approved write-offs are booked at once and the physical goods are disposed only to the approved route. Restock is prohibited for written-off lines. Rework in Zone F is allowed only where the supervisor has approved it as safe and saleable, otherwise the goods are scrapped, with hazmat and chilled scrap handled to instruction and waste cleared to its point.

9. Safety and segregation apply through quarantine and disposal. All work observes high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear, 10 km/h inside the hall and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps. Spills follow PR-13, cold-chain failures follow PR-12, and rack storage aisles of 3.0 m, main aisles of 4.0 m and walkways of 1.2 m behind yellow barriers are kept clear.

10. Every quarantine, recount, proposal, approval, write-off posting and disposal is entered in the system and shift record before handover. Product, batch, quantities, values, checker and approver names and quarantine references are recorded, and open quarantines and pending manager approvals are carried into the end-of-shift handover under PR-15 until closed and filed.

title: Fleet and Authorisation
text:
1. All materials-handling trucks on site are electric. The fleet comprises 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t for general work, 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t for the high bays in Zone B, 8 electric pallet jacks for powered small moves, and 12 hand pallet jacks for manual small moves. No diesel, gas or other fuelled trucks are used.

2. Counterbalance forklifts handle general transport across Zones A to D and Zone F, including unloading support, put-away to block stacks, replenishment running, and staging and loading in Zone D. They do not work the high-bay rack faces above their rated height and capacity, which remain reach-truck work.

3. Reach trucks work the high-bay pallet racking in Zone B providing 2,400 pallet positions. They place and retrieve only directed, labelled pallets within the 1,000 kg maximum per pallet load included and the 2,700 kg maximum per rack bay. They are not used for dispatch running or yard work.

4. Electric pallet jacks serve powered horizontal moves in Zone A receiving, Zone C picking and Zone D staging, and hand pallet jacks serve small, short moves by trained staff. Both types move only stable, labelled units within the 1,000 kg pallet limit and never lift to rack height.

5. The wider equipment pool supports the fleet but is not driven as trucks. Dispatch runs 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers for outbound pallets, the site operates 1 cardboard baler for waste, each of the 8 dock doors has its own leveller, and the teams share 20 handheld WMS scanners for all bookings and confirmations.

6. Only forklift operators drive forklifts and reach trucks. Inbound operators, pickers, stock controllers, returns and packing staff, dispatchers and floaters do not drive these trucks unless they hold the same authorisation and are rostered as operators for that shift under the shift supervisor.

7. No licence means no truck. Every forklift and reach-truck operator holds a valid licence for the truck type driven, completed site training on our electric fleet, aisles, racking and pedestrian rules, and a current authorisation recorded by management before driving unsupervised.

8. Only the warehouse manager authorises new forklift operators. Shift supervisors, dispatchers, the maintenance technician and other staff do not grant driving permission, extend an authorisation to another truck type, or approve visitors, drivers or agency staff to drive. Unauthorised driving is stopped and reported as an incident.

9. Authorisation is truck-specific and remains under review. The manager records operator name, licence, truck types covered, date of authorisation and refresher due date. Any incident, near miss, damage to racking or dock equipment, or observed unsafe driving suspends driving until the manager and shift supervisor have reviewed and re-authorised.

10. Every truck gets a documented check before its first use each day under PR-10. The operator due to drive it checks brakes, steering, forks, chains, guards, lights, horn, seat belt, battery charge and leaks, records the result with truck identity, date, time and name, and reports any defect to the shift supervisor and maintenance technician. A failed or unrecorded truck is not used until cleared.

title: Daily Checks and Maintenance
text:
1. Every truck gets a documented check before its first use each day under PR-10. The check applies to the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t, the 8 electric pallet jacks and the 12 hand pallet jacks. A truck without a recorded pass for that day is not used.

2. The check is done by the operator due to drive the truck first on that shift, mornings 06:00-14:00 or afternoons 14:00-22:00. The operator uses the standard check sheet on paper or the handheld WMS scanner, records truck identity, date, time and name, and signs the result before moving any load.

3. The daily check covers the full working condition. Brakes, parking brake, steering, forks and carriage, chains and hoses, guards and backrest, lights, beacon, horn, reversing alarm, seat belt, battery charge and connector, tyres and wheels, leaks and panel damage are all inspected. For pallet jacks the tiller, lift and lower, wheels and handle brake are checked in the same way.

4. Any defect fails the truck. The operator marks the sheet as failed, removes the key or disables the tiller, attaches a do-not-use tag, and reports at once to the shift supervisor in charge of the floor and to the maintenance technician. A failed truck is parked clear of the 4.0 m main aisles, 3.0 m rack aisles and pedestrian walkways until cleared.

5. Minor faults that still allow safe holding, such as a damaged label, mirror or horn fault, stop driving until repaired or exempted in writing for one shift only. Brake, steering, fork, chain, guard, seat-belt or battery faults never receive an exemption. No licence means no truck, and no check means no truck.

6. The maintenance technician owns all repairs to trucks, racking and dock equipment. The technician assesses every reported defect the same shift, makes the truck safe, carries out the repair or isolates it with barriering, and decides whether it may return to service. Floor staff do not repair, bypass or reset trucks themselves.

7. Every repair is logged. The log records date and time reported, truck identity, defect found, daily-check reference, action taken, parts replaced, time returned to service and technician name. Check sheets, failed tags and repair entries are filed together and open items are carried into the end-of-shift handover under PR-15 until closed.

8. Planned maintenance is carried out to schedule without stopping flow. The technician plans battery charging and rotation, tyre, fork and chain inspections, servicing of the electric fleet, and checks of the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers, the cardboard baler and the 8 dock levellers. Worn or overdue trucks are withdrawn before the shift starts.

9. Dock levellers, wrappers and shared equipment are checked with the same discipline. Levellers are tested by trained staff before call-forward to Doors 1-8, wrapper turntables, films and guards are checked before packing, and any defect to a door, leveller, seal, wrapper or baler is reported immediately to maintenance and the dispatcher and logged as a repair.

10. The shift supervisor reviews every check failure and repair on the shift before it is closed or escalated to the warehouse manager. Truck impacts, racking strikes, dropped pallets and near misses are reported as incidents, the scene is preserved, and driving is suspended until the manager and supervisor have reviewed and re-authorised. Completed checks and closed repairs are confirmed in the handover.

title: Safe Driving Rules
text:
1. All truck driving on site runs under PR-10 and PR-11. Only authorised forklift operators drive the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t and the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t, and only trained staff use the 8 electric and 12 hand pallet jacks. No licence means no truck, and no truck moves without a documented check passed for that day.

2. Speed limits are enforced on every move. The limit is 10 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the fenced yard, and 5 km/h wherever people and trucks meet — marked pedestrian zones, crossings, and the dock ramps and approaches to Doors 1-8. Operators slow to walking pace at blind corners, rack ends, cold-store doors and the Zone F cage entrance.

3. Operators drive only on marked truck routes and keep to the aisle discipline. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide and rack storage aisles in Zone B are 3.0 m wide, marked and kept clear. Nothing is driven onto the 1.2 m pedestrian walkways behind yellow barriers, across staging lanes, or outside the assigned zone flow.

4. Pedestrians have priority at every crossing. Operators stop and give way at all marked crossings, pedestrian zones and dock ramps, sound the horn at junctions and doors, keep lights and beacon on where fitted, and never overtake or crowd pedestrians. Pedestrians use only walkways and crossings and never ride on trucks or pallets.

5. Seat belts and protective equipment are mandatory on every trip. Forklift operators wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving, and all floor staff wear high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear. Operators never drive with the belt bypassed, the guards removed, or the load blocking forward view without driving in reverse under guidance.

6. Every load respects the rated capacity of the truck and the pallet limit. No pallet, load included, may weigh more than 1,000 kg. Operators check the label and system weight before lifting, stay within the 2.5 t counterbalance and 1.6 t reach ratings with height derating, and refuse overweight, unstable, overhanging or damaged pallets.

7. Racking and stacking limits are observed from the seat. Each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg in total, and block stacks stand only in marked areas limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m total height together. Operators confirm the bay before placing, set pallets square without impact, and never push, drag or double-handle racked pallets.

8. Loads are carried low, stable and secure. Forks are kept low for travel, tilted back, with the heaviest weight low and centred and the film and labels intact. Operators never travel with raised forks, carry loose cartons on forks, lift people, tow trailers or levellers, or park with a raised load in an aisle, across a crossing, or on a ramp.

9. Dock, yard and parking discipline applies to every truck. Operators approach Doors 1-4 and 5-8 only on dispatcher and supervisor instruction, stop clear of the leveller until the vehicle is braked and secured, and observe the 5 km/h dock limit. At shift end trucks are parked in their points, braked, lowered, switched off with keys removed, and left clear of exits and fire equipment.

10. Any impact, drop, scrape to racking, leveller fault or near miss stops driving at once. The operator makes the area safe, reports to the shift supervisor in charge of the floor and to the maintenance technician, and preserves the scene for review. Driving resumes only after inspection, repair logging, and re-authorisation, and every event is recorded and carried into the end-of-shift handover under PR-15.

title: Aisles and Walkways
text:
1. All vehicle and pedestrian movement inside the hall and in the fenced yard runs on marked, separated routes. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide, rack storage aisles in Zone B are 3.0 m wide, and pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide and physically separated by yellow barriers. No route is narrowed, moved or removed without instruction.

2. Main transport aisles of 4.0 m carry forklift, reach-truck and pallet-jack traffic between Zones A to F and to Doors 1-8. They are marked on the floor with edge lines, direction arrows and crossing points, and are kept clear at all times for manoeuvre and visibility. Nothing is stored, staged or parked in a main aisle.

3. Rack storage aisles of 3.0 m serve the high-bay racking in Zone B with its 2,400 pallet positions and the ground-level faces in Zone C. They allow one truck to work the face with safe clearance to the racking on both sides. Pallets, film, waste and equipment are never left standing in a rack aisle, across a rack face or at a rack end.

4. Pedestrian walkways of 1.2 m are provided along the main transport routes, around Zones A, B, C, D and F, and on approach to the office annex, waiting area, cold-store doors and dock areas. They are physically separated from truck lanes by continuous yellow barriers, marked with walking symbols, and used by all staff on foot.

5. Barriers, markings and signage are permanent site furniture. Yellow barriers, floor lines, crossing zebra marks, mirror heads at blind corners, and zone and door signs are inspected daily by the shift team and maintained by the maintenance technician. Any missing, damaged or obscured barrier, line or sign is reported at once and made safe the same shift.

6. Pedestrians and trucks meet only at marked crossings, pedestrian zones and dock ramps. Pedestrians cross truck lanes only at marked zebra crossings with clear sight lines, stop and look before stepping out, and give trucks time to stop. Operators stop and give way at every crossing and sound the horn at junctions, doors and blind corners.

7. Aisles, walkways, dock approaches and emergency routes are kept free of obstruction through every shift. Access to dock levellers at Doors 1-8, emergency exits, fire equipment, first-aid points, the 2 stretch wrappers, the hazmat cage entrance and the Zone E cold doors is never blocked by pallets, cages, waste or parked trucks.

8. Zone discipline protects the routes. Zone A receiving, Zone B bulk with block stacks limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m together, Zone C picking, Zone D staging by door and load, Zone E cold store and Zone F services with its 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage all hold their goods inside marked boundaries. Overspill into an aisle or walkway is moved back immediately.

9. The yard follows the same separation outside the hall. Marked manoeuvring lanes serve dock approach, the driver waiting area is separated from reversing trucks, and pedestrians use only marked walkways to the office annex and waiting area. Drivers wait in the designated area until called forward and never wait in the hall or on dock approaches.

10. Every blockage, damage to barriers or racking, spill, or near miss on an aisle, walkway or crossing is reported to the shift supervisor in charge of the floor and recorded for review. The affected lane is barriered and cleared before normal flow resumes, and open items are carried into the end-of-shift handover under PR-15. Pedestrian safety rules in full run under PR-11.

title: Speed Limits
text:
1. Three speed limits apply to every vehicle movement on site, and every driver observes them without exception. The limit is 10 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the fenced yard, and 5 km/h wherever people and trucks meet — marked pedestrian zones, crossings, and the dock ramps and approaches to Doors 1-8. The 5 km/h limit overrides the higher limit wherever it applies.

2. The 10 km/h inside limit covers all trucks inside the hall. The 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t, and the 8 electric and 12 hand pallet jacks observe 10 km/h on the 4.0 m main transport aisles and in Zones A to F. No higher speed is used to clear backlog, and no supervisor instruction overrides the limit.

3. The 15 km/h yard limit covers all movements in the 3,500 m2 fenced yard. Contracted curtain-side trailers, the delivery van, and any internal truck crossing the yard observe 15 km/h on the marked manoeuvring lanes and dock approaches. Drivers slow before turns, gates, the waiting area and parked vehicles, and give way at every marked pedestrian crossing.

4. The 5 km/h shared-area limit covers every place where pedestrians and vehicles meet. It applies at all zebra crossings, along the 1.2 m pedestrian walkways behind yellow barriers, in pedestrian zones, at the office annex and waiting-area routes, at rack ends and blind corners, at the Zone E cold doors, at the Zone F cage entrance, and on all dock ramps. Operators slow to walking pace and stop to give way.

5. Limits are signed and marked where they apply. Speed roundels, floor markings, crossing zebra marks, mirror heads at blind corners, and door and ramp signage show the limit at hall entries, yard entries, crossings and dock approaches. Signs are inspected daily by the shift team and maintained by the maintenance technician, and any missing or obscured sign is reported and made safe the same shift.

6. Reversing, manoeuvring and dock work run at or below 5 km/h. Reversing to Doors 1-4 and Doors 5-8 is done slowly on mirrors, with guidance from the inbound or dispatch team where provided, and only after dispatcher call-forward. No vehicle reverses across a pedestrian route without a clear lookout, horn signal and full stop for pedestrians.

7. Operators adjust below the posted limit for load and conditions. Heavy pallets up to the 1,000 kg maximum per pallet load included, high or long loads, wet or uneven floors, poor visibility, congestion in the 3.0 m rack storage aisles, and work near staging in Zone D or receiving in Zone A all require slower driving, forks low and tilted back, and lights and beacon on where fitted.

8. Pedestrian priority enforces the limits at every meeting point. Operators stop and give way at all crossings, sound the horn at junctions, doors and blind corners, and never overtake or crowd pedestrians. Pedestrians use only walkways and crossings and never ride on trucks or pallets. Seat belts remain worn whenever the truck is moving, and high-visibility vests and class S3 footwear are worn on the floor.

9. Speeding, dangerous driving and failure to give way stop driving at once. The operator or driver is stopped by the shift supervisor in charge of the floor, the area is made safe, and the event is reported as an incident under PR-10 and PR-11. Authorisation to drive remains suspended until the warehouse manager and supervisor have reviewed, and repairs to racking, barriers or dock equipment are logged by maintenance.

10. Every speeding event, near miss, barrier or racking strike, and leveller or signage defect is recorded before handover. Date, time, location, vehicle and driver identity, limit applying and action taken are entered in the shift record, and open items are carried into the end-of-shift handover under PR-15 until closed. Limits apply in full on both shifts, mornings 06:00-14:00 and afternoons 14:00-22:00, and on any approved Saturday morning overtime.

title: PPE and Pedestrians
text:
1. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, no exceptions. The rule covers all Zones A to F, all aisles, dock areas inside the building, and any entry to Zone E cold store and the Zone F hazmat cage. No one starts work, enters the floor, or remains on the floor without both items correctly worn.

2. Forklift operators wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving. The belt is fastened before the truck moves off, stays fastened for the whole trip including short repositioning in Zone A, Zone B, Zone C and Zone D, and is only released after the truck is braked and parked. Driving with the belt bypassed, removed or faulty stops driving at once.

3. Pedestrians move only on the marked pedestrian system under PR-11. The 1.2 m walkways physically separated by yellow barriers are used for all movement on foot along main transport routes, around Zones A, B, C, D and F, and to the office annex, cold-store doors and dock areas. Stepping into the 4.0 m main aisles or 3.0 m rack aisles except at marked crossings is prohibited.

4. Trucks and pedestrians meet only at marked points. Pedestrians cross truck lanes only at zebra crossings with clear sight lines, stop and look before stepping out, make eye contact with the operator, and give trucks time to stop. Operators stop and give way at every crossing, pedestrian zone and dock ramp, sound the horn at junctions, doors and blind corners, and observe 5 km/h at all these points.

5. Pedestrian priority applies in full at shared areas. Marked pedestrian zones, crossings, the office annex and waiting-area routes, rack ends and blind corners, the Zone E cold doors, the Zone F cage entrance, and all dock ramps and approaches to Doors 1-8 are 5 km/h areas. Pedestrians never ride on trucks, forks or pallets, never walk under raised forks, and never enter a barriered rack bay or dock working area.

6. Drivers and visitors follow the same pedestrian control. They report to the office annex on arrival, wait in the marked waiting area in the fenced yard until called, and never wait in the hall, on dock approaches or in manoeuvring lanes. They enter the operational floor only when authorised and escorted, wearing high-visibility vests and class S3 footwear, and stay in the designated safe position during loading and unloading.

7. Condition and cleanliness of PPE and barriers are checked every shift. Staff check vests for visibility and fastening and footwear for sole, toe cap and closure before starting, and replace damaged items the same shift through the shift supervisor. Yellow barriers, floor lines, crossing marks, mirrors and signs are inspected daily, and any missing, damaged or obscured barrier or marking is reported to the shift supervisor and maintenance technician and made safe the same shift.

8. Behaviour around trucks is disciplined at all times. Pedestrians keep clear of reversing vehicles, turning circles and trailer swing, do not pass behind a reversing truck, do not use mobile phones while crossing, and carry loads so sight lines stay open. Operators keep lights and beacon on where fitted, drive forks low with the load tilted back, and never overtake or crowd pedestrians in aisles or at doors.

9. Any failure of PPE or pedestrian discipline stops the work. Missing vest or footwear, unbelted driving, walking outside walkways, crossing away from markings, riding on equipment, or entering an unauthorised zone is stopped by the shift supervisor in charge of the floor, made safe, and reported as an incident. Driving authorisation remains suspended until the warehouse manager and supervisor have reviewed.

10. Every PPE issue, pedestrian near miss, barrier defect and enforcement action is recorded before handover. Date, time, location, persons and vehicles involved, and action taken are entered in the shift record, repairs are logged by maintenance, and open items are carried into the end-of-shift handover under PR-15 until closed. The rules apply in full on both shifts, mornings 06:00-14:00 and afternoons 14:00-22:00, and on any approved Saturday morning overtime.

title: Evacuation and Drills
text:
1. Evacuation on site runs under PR-14 and applies to everyone in the hall, office annex and fenced yard. On alarm, all receiving, put-away, replenishment, picking, packing, dispatch, counting and maintenance work stops at once, and the building is evacuated without delay for people, stock or equipment.

2. Any person discovering fire, smoke, gas release, major spill, structural failure or other danger raises the alarm at the nearest call point and notifies the shift supervisor in charge of the floor at once. The supervisor secures people first, calls the required emergency support, and escalates to the warehouse manager without delay.

3. Evacuation uses only marked emergency routes and exits. Main transport aisles of 4.0 m, rack storage aisles of 3.0 m, pedestrian walkways of 1.2 m behind yellow barriers, dock approaches and emergency exits are kept clear at all times so routes stay passable. Nothing is stored, staged or parked across an exit, leveller, fire point or aisle.

4. On alarm, operators brake trucks where safe clear of aisles, crossings and exits, lower forks, switch off and leave keys in place, and leave on foot. Staff leave pallets, scanners and paperwork, close Zone E cold doors and the Zone F cage where it is safe to do so without delaying exit, and do not use lifts, trucks or pallet jacks to evacuate.

5. All evacuees move on foot by the marked walkways and crossings to the assembly point by the north fence, keeping clear of manoeuvring lanes and dock reversing areas. Running, re-entering for belongings, and crossing in front of emergency vehicles are prohibited. High-visibility vests and class S3 footwear remain worn at assembly.

6. Roll call at the assembly point by the north fence happens before anyone re-enters the building. The shift supervisor on duty leads the roll call with shift lists, visitor and driver logs from the office annex, and count-team sheets, checking off warehouse staff, floaters, maintenance, dispatch, drivers and escorted visitors by name.

7. Drivers waiting in the marked waiting area and any visitors in the office annex evacuate with staff direction to the same north-fence assembly point and remain there for roll call. No driver moves a trailer or van during evacuation, and no vehicle blocks gates, hydrants or emergency access in the 3,500 m2 yard.

8. No one re-enters the hall, annex or dock areas until the all-clear is given. The shift supervisor secures the perimeter, prevents re-entry, and reports missing or unaccounted persons to the emergency services at once. Re-entry is authorised only when the building is declared safe, and staff return only to directed zones and tasks.

9. An evacuation drill is run every quarter under PR-14 across both shifts, mornings 06:00-14:00 and afternoons 14:00-22:00, including any Saturday morning overtime crew where rostered. Each drill tests alarm, route discipline, truck shutdown, movement to the north fence, roll call and re-entry control, with performance timed and observed.

10. Every alarm, evacuation and drill is recorded before handover. Date, time, location, cause, time to clear the building, roll-call result, missing-person actions, defects to alarms, exits, barriers or signage, and the re-entry authorisation are entered in the shift record, reviewed by the shift supervisor in every incident report, and carried into the end-of-shift handover under PR-15 until closed.

title: Incident Response
text:
1. Every incident on site gets an immediate floor response under PR-14 and PR-15, led by the shift supervisor in charge of the floor. Injury, fire alarm, spill, leak, cold-chain alarm, racking strike, truck impact, dropped pallet, damage to goods, near miss and security issue all count as incidents and are dealt with on the shift they happen.

2. Any person discovering an incident makes the area safe as far as possible without taking risk, stops the work around it, and notifies the shift supervisor at once. Operators brake trucks clear of aisles, crossings and exits, lower forks and switch off, pedestrians move to the 1.2 m walkways behind yellow barriers, and first aid or spill containment starts only where it is safe to do so.

3. The shift supervisor secures people first, then goods and equipment. The supervisor directs floor staff, calls the maintenance technician, emergency services or other support as needed, isolates the bay, aisle, door or cage involved, and prevents further put-away, replenishment, picking or dispatch through the affected area until it is cleared.

4. The scene is preserved for review. Racking, pallets, trucks, levellers, labels, scanner records and temperature logs are left as found, photographs are taken where required, and witnesses, vehicle and driver identity, location, date and time are recorded. Cleaning, repair or restacking starts only on supervisor instruction.

5. Escalation to the warehouse manager happens without delay. The supervisor reports what happened, who is affected, what is secured and what support is on the way, and carries out manager instructions on shutdown, medical follow-up, customer notification and stock hold. Open stock issues and overtime need arising from the incident go through the same line.

6. Damaged goods arising from an incident go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09. Affected pallets are labelled with product, quantity, batch, location, damage type and finder name, segregated from correct stock and scan-recorded as quarantine, not as available stock. No damaged line is restocked, reworked or counted as available without approval.

7. Hazmat and cold-chain incidents follow their dedicated rules together with the general response. Spills and leaks at the ventilated 60 m2 cage in Zone F follow PR-13 with ventilation, spill kits and safety data sheets, and temperature excursions outside +2 °C to +8 °C in Zone E follow PR-12 with record preservation. Incompatible hazmat classes are never combined during making-safe.

8. Every incident is written up as an incident report on the shift. The report records date, time, location in Zones A to F, persons and vehicles involved, description, immediate action, quarantine references, witnesses and repair needs. Check failures, barrier or racking damage and speeding or pedestrian breaches are recorded with the limit applying and action taken.

9. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report arising on the shift before it is closed or escalated to the warehouse manager. The supervisor checks facts against scanner history and handover records, confirms quarantine, recount and repair logging, directs follow-up replenishment or staging, and suspends driving or zone access until re-authorisation where the rules require it.

10. All reports, reviews, repairs and follow-up actions are entered in the system and shift record before handover. Open incidents, barriered bays, quarantined lines, pending manager sign-offs for write-offs above 500 EUR and the annual stocktake, and any restriction on doors, trucks or aisles are carried into the end-of-shift handover under PR-15 until closed, with PPE, seat-belt and speed rules — 10 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps — applying throughout.

title: Handover and Shifts
text:
1. The site operates two fixed shifts, Monday to Friday, mornings 06:00-14:00 and afternoons 14:00-22:00. All routine work in Zones A to F is planned inside these windows. In peak season Saturday morning overtime may be added to clear backlog, and no regular Sunday or night working is operated.

2. There is always one shift supervisor in charge of the floor during operating hours. The morning supervisor runs the 06:00-14:00 floor and the afternoon supervisor runs the 14:00-22:00 floor. Floor staff report to the supervisor on duty for tasking, safety and incident reporting, and the supervisor reports to the warehouse manager.

3. Every shift ends with a formal end-of-shift handover under PR-15. The outgoing shift supervisor leads the handover to the incoming supervisor, with stock controllers, dispatchers and the maintenance technician contributing their areas. No shift is left without a recorded handover, including the close of afternoon to next morning and the close to any approved Saturday overtime.

4. The handover covers status by zone and flow. Zone A bookings and waiting vehicles, put-away to Zones B, E and the hazmat cage, Zone C replenishment and open picks, Zone D staging by door and load with releases and seals, Zone E temperature readings, Zone F returns, quarantine and rework, and daily cycle counts with recounts and pending adjustments are all stated with system references.

5. Open items are carried forward until closed. Open incidents, barriered rack bays, failed trucks, door or leveller faults, quarantined lines, pending write-off approvals, delayed carriers and door conflicts are entered in the shift record with location, action taken and owner, and appear in the next handover until repair, recount, approval or release closes them.

6. Only the warehouse manager approves overtime. Shift supervisors identify the need, roster the 2 floaters within the shift, and reprioritise Zones A to F, but they do not authorise additional hours, additional shifts, extended opening or Saturday working on their own authority.

7. Saturday morning overtime is overtime only and is planned in advance. The manager defines the date, morning window, roster and tasks, and the dispatcher books only the doors and slots covered by that approval. Performance against the 288 full-weight pallet per shift ceiling, door throughput of 3 trailer loads per door, and handover discipline apply in full.

8. Shift-start and shift-end checks are part of the handover. Every truck gets a documented check before its first use each day, the manual Zone E verification between +2 °C and +8 °C is done and recorded on every shift, barriers, markings, walkways of 1.2 m behind yellow barriers, aisles of 4.0 m and 3.0 m, and dock levellers at Doors 1-8 are confirmed clear, and defects are reported to maintenance and logged.

9. Staffing, PPE and safety discipline are confirmed at handover. Attendance, absence cover by floaters, authorised forklift operators only with no licence meaning no truck, high-visibility vests and class S3 footwear, seat belts whenever trucks move, and speed limits of 10 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps are checked and any breach is recorded as an incident.

10. Every handover is scan-recorded and filed before flow resumes. Date, time, outgoing and incoming supervisor names, counts, bookings, releases, seals, alarms, drills with roll call at the north fence, and open-item carry-forwards are entered in the system and shift record under PR-15, reviewed by the incoming supervisor, and escalated to the warehouse manager where a manager-only sign-off is required.

title: Forklift Operating Rules
text:
1. Only authorised forklift operators may drive powered materials-handling equipment on site. Authorisation is given personally by the warehouse manager, and no other person, including shift supervisors, may approve a new operator.

2. Authorisation applies only after the operator holds a valid licence for the truck type and has completed site familiarisation. Without a current licence, no truck of any kind may be driven.

3. The 8 designated forklift operators are the only staff who routinely drive the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t and the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t. They are also permitted to operate the 8 electric pallet jacks.

4. Other trained floor staff may use the 12 hand pallet jacks and, where specifically trained, electric pallet jacks for small moves only. They may never operate a counterbalance forklift or a reach truck.

5. Reach trucks are the only trucks permitted to work in the high-bay racking in Zone B bulk storage. Counterbalance forklifts are used for general work, unloading and loading at the docks, and transport on the main aisles.

6. No truck may be used for its first task of the day until its documented daily check has been completed. The check is recorded in writing and covers brakes, steering, horn, lights, forks, chains, tyres, battery charge and safety devices.

7. If the daily check reveals any defect, the truck is taken out of service immediately, tagged, and reported to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician. No makeshift repair or continued use is permitted, and every repair is logged by the maintenance technician.

8. Speed limits are mandatory and are enforced as follows: 10 km/h maximum inside the building, 15 km/h maximum in the yard, and 5 km/h maximum wherever people and trucks may meet, including marked pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps.

9. The driver must reduce speed further below the posted limit when visibility is restricted, at aisle intersections, when entering or leaving Zones A, C and D, and when operating in the 3.0 m rack storage aisles or the 4.0 m main transport aisles with pedestrians nearby.

10. Seat belts must be worn by forklift operators whenever the truck is moving, without exception. The belt is fastened before moving off and remains fastened until the truck is fully parked.

11. Loads must never exceed the rated capacity of the truck or the 1,000 kg maximum weight per pallet including load. Overweight, unstable or visibly damaged pallets must not be lifted until they have been made safe.

12. Forks are carried low, tilted slightly back, and clear of the floor during travel. Loaded trucks travel with the load facing uphill on ramps, and no person is ever carried as a passenger or lifted on the forks.

13. The driver must give way to pedestrians at all times, sound the horn at crossings, blind corners and dock areas, and stop completely where sight lines are blocked. Pedestrian walkways separated by yellow barriers must never be driven on or blocked.

14. Trucks are parked only in their marked parking positions with forks lowered to the floor, controls in neutral, parking brake applied and power switched off. Keys or access devices are never left in an unattended truck.

15. All forklift and MHE operation follows procedure PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation together with PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse. Any breach of authorisation, speed, seat-belt or daily-check rules is reported immediately to the shift supervisor in charge of the floor.

title: Pedestrian Walkways and Crossings
text:
1. All pedestrian movement inside the hall uses only the designated walkways. These walkways are 1.2 m wide and are physically separated from truck routes by yellow barriers along their full length.

2. No person may walk in the 4.0 m main transport aisles, in the 3.0 m rack storage aisles in Zone B, or in any operating area as a shortcut. Pedestrians stay behind the barriers except where a marked crossing is provided.

3. Walkways, crossings, stairways and exits are kept clear at all times. Pallets, wrapping material, scanners, jacks and waste are never placed on a walkway or in front of a barrier opening, even for a short stop.

4. Every crossing of a truck route is made only at a marked pedestrian crossing. Before stepping onto a crossing, the pedestrian stops, looks both ways, makes eye contact with any approaching driver, and waits for the truck to stop completely.

5. Where people and trucks may meet — marked pedestrian zones, all crossings, and the dock ramps at doors 1-8 — trucks are limited to 5 km/h. Pedestrians remain aware that this limit does not remove the need to check before crossing.

6. Drivers give way to pedestrians at crossings, blind corners and dock areas. Pedestrians must still never assume they have been seen and must never step out from behind racking, stacked pallets or a parked trailer into the path of a truck.

7. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, including on walkways and crossings, with no exceptions. Dark, worn or damaged vests that reduce visibility are replaced immediately.

8. Extra care is required at the entrances to Zone A receiving, Zone C picking and Zone D dispatch, where forklift and pallet-jack traffic is continuous. Pedestrians use only the barrier-protected entries and crossings and follow any floor markings and mirrors provided.

9. In Zone B bulk storage, pedestrians use the designated walkways to reach the rack aisles and do not walk the length of a 3.0 m storage aisle alongside an operating reach truck. If a reach truck is working in an aisle, the pedestrian waits at the aisle entry until the operator signals it is safe.

10. Dock ramps, levellers and the staging areas in front of doors 1-8 are truck operating areas, not pedestrian routes. Pedestrians enter these areas only for an assigned task, use the marked pedestrian lanes, and keep clear of reversing vehicles and lowering levellers.

11. Carriers and visitors do not enter the hall on foot. Drivers wait in the marked waiting area in the yard and enter the site only when instructed by the dispatcher for a supervised loading or unloading activity with an escort.

12. Running is prohibited on walkways, crossings and in all zones. Mobile phones and handheld WMS scanners are not used while crossing a truck route; the pedestrian stops in a safe place behind the barrier before reading or entering data.

13. Damaged barriers, faded walkway lines, missing crossing markings, defective lighting or blocked sight lines are reported at once to the shift supervisor in charge of the floor and to the maintenance technician for repair and logging.

14. All pedestrian movement follows procedure PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse together with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Any near miss, barrier strike or breach of walkway and crossing rules is reported immediately to the shift supervisor for review.

title: Yard and Dock Safety
text:
1. The fenced yard of 3,500 m2 is a controlled traffic area. All vehicle movements in the yard follow the door and time slot assigned by the dispatcher, and no carrier enters the yard or approaches a dock without a confirmed slot.

2. Dock doors are strictly segregated. Doors 1-4 are inbound only for unloading in Zone A receiving, and doors 5-8 are outbound only for loading from Zone D dispatch. No inbound truck is sent to an outbound door and no outbound truck to an inbound door.

3. Drivers report on arrival and wait in the marked waiting area in the yard. Drivers never enter the hall unescorted and never proceed to a door until called forward by the dispatcher for supervised loading or unloading.

4. The speed limit in the yard is 15 km/h maximum. On the dock ramps, at marked pedestrian zones and crossings, and wherever people and trucks may meet, the limit is 5 km/h maximum. The 10 km/h limit applies as soon as a truck or MHE is inside the building.

5. Pedestrians in the yard use only marked pedestrian lanes, walkways and crossings. Drivers give way to pedestrians at all times, and no person walks behind a reversing vehicle or between a trailer and the dock.

6. Reversing to the 1.2 m high docks is done slowly, with mirrors, reversing aids and a banksman where visibility is restricted. No person stands in the crush zone between the trailer and the dock wall or leveller while the vehicle is docking.

7. A trailer is only approached for loading or unloading when it is fully stopped, braked and secured at its assigned door, with the engine switched off and the driver notified. The vehicle does not move until loading or unloading is confirmed complete and all staff and equipment are clear.

8. Each of the 8 dock doors has its own dock leveller. Only trained, authorised staff operate a leveller, and no leveller is operated while persons or MHE are on the ramp edge or in the path of the plate.

9. Before driving onto a leveller, the operator checks that the trailer bed is aligned, the leveller plate is fully seated on the trailer, and the combined weight of truck, pallet and load is within the leveller and the 1,000 kg maximum per pallet. Any gap, bounce, oil leak or faulty lip is reported at once.

10. Forklifts and pallet jacks cross between dock and trailer only over a correctly seated leveller, at walking pace and within the 5 km/h dock-ramp limit. Forks are kept low, loads tilted slightly back, and sudden braking or turning on the leveller plate is prohibited.

11. Dock edges, levellers and staging areas in front of doors 1-8 are truck operating areas. Pallets, wrap, waste and unused equipment are never stored on the ramp, on leveller controls, in front of doors, or in yard traffic lanes.

12. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for everyone on the docks and in the yard operating areas, with no exceptions. Seat belts remain fastened whenever a forklift is moving on the dock and ramp.

13. Damaged dock doors, levellers, bumpers, yard markings, lighting, fencing or barriers are reported immediately to the shift supervisor in charge of the floor and to the maintenance technician for repair and logging. A defective door or leveller is taken out of use until repaired.

14. All yard and dock work follows procedure PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation together with PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse and PR-06 Outbound dispatch and PR-01 Inbound receiving as applicable. Any near miss, barrier strike, unauthorised entry or breach of door-assignment, speed or leveller rules is reported immediately to the shift supervisor and to the dispatcher.

title: Mandatory PPE
text:
1. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, without exception. No person enters or remains in Zones A to F, on the docks, or in yard operating areas without both items correctly worn.

2. The rule applies equally to all staff, including the warehouse manager, shift supervisors, office staff visiting the floor, maintenance staff, and any escorted visitor or contractor. Rank, short duration, or familiarity with the site does not exempt any person.

3. Vests are worn closed and fastened over outer clothing at all times on the floor, so that the reflective bands remain visible from the front, back and sides. Jackets, bags, or carried goods must never cover the vest while in truck operating areas.

4. Only clean, intact, high-visibility vests with fully reflective strips are acceptable. Faded, torn, heavily soiled, or darkened vests that reduce visibility are replaced immediately and are not used on the floor.

5. Footwear means safety shoes or boots of class S3, fully laced or fastened, worn with socks. Open shoes, trainers, sandals, or any non-safety footwear are prohibited on the warehouse floor, on the docks, and in marked yard operating areas.

6. Footwear must be intact, with undamaged toe caps, soles, and fastenings. Worn soles, split uppers, missing laces, or water-damaged shoes are taken out of use and replaced before the next shift on the floor.

7. Each employee is responsible for arriving on shift with compliant vest and footwear and for checking their condition before entering the hall. The shift supervisor in charge of the floor enforces compliance and refuses floor access to anyone non-compliant.

8. Carriers and external drivers remain in the marked waiting area in the yard and do not enter the hall unescorted. Where a driver is instructed by the dispatcher to take part in a supervised loading or unloading activity, vest and S3 footwear are required for the dock and hall areas.

9. Spare compliant vests are kept available at the floor entrances for supervised visitors who have no personal vest. No visitor footwear other than class S3 is accepted for entry to operating areas; visitors without compliant footwear do not enter the floor.

10. Seat belts are mandatory for forklift operators whenever the truck is moving. The belt is fastened before moving off from parking, from a dock, or after any stop, and remains fastened until the truck is fully parked with the brake applied.

11. The seat-belt rule applies to all movements inside the building and in the yard, including short repositioning, travel on the 4.0 m main aisles, work on dock ramps at the 5 km/h limit, and travel with or without a load. No standing start without a fastened belt is permitted.

12. A truck with a missing, damaged, or non-locking seat belt is taken out of service immediately, tagged, and reported to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician. The truck is not returned to use until the belt is repaired and logged.

13. Deliberate non-use, modification, or disabling of a seat belt is treated as a breach of procedure PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Passengers are never carried, so no additional belts or makeshift seating are permitted on any truck.

14. Any breach of vest, footwear, or seat-belt rules, any shortage of spare vests, and any defective PPE found during the shift is reported at once to the shift supervisor in charge of the floor. PPE compliance is checked as part of daily supervision and end-of-shift handover under PR-15.

title: Racking and Stacking Limits
text:
1. All pallet storage in Zone B bulk storage uses only the designated high-bay pallet racking or approved block-stack areas. No pallets are stored free-standing in aisles, on walkways, in front of dock doors, or against barriers and exits.

2. A single pallet including its load may weigh at most 1,000 kg. This 1,000 kg figure is the basis for every rack and stacking limit on site, and no overweight pallet is placed into racking or onto a block stack.

3. Each rack bay in the high-bay racking may carry at most 2,700 kg in total across all levels in that bay. The limit applies to the combined weight of pallets, loads and packaging within the bay, not per level.

4. In practice the 2,700 kg bay limit means no more than two full-weight 1,000 kg pallets plus normal variation may share one bay, and three full-weight pallets are never placed in the same bay. Stock controllers and forklift operators check weights in the WMS task before put-away.

5. Free block-stacking outside the racking is limited to 3 pallets high and to 4.0 m total height including the pallets and load. Neither limit may be exceeded, so the lower of the two always applies for high or unstable loads.

6. Block stacks are placed only on level, marked floor areas able to take the weight, never in the 3.0 m rack storage aisles, the 4.0 m main transport aisles, pedestrian walkways, crossings, or dock staging areas in front of doors 1-8.

7. Pallets placed in racking or in block stacks must be intact, correctly wrapped and stable, with the load evenly distributed and within the pallet footprint. Damaged, leaning, split, overhanging or unwrapped pallets are not stored at height until they have been re-wrapped or re-palletised.

8. Only the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t are permitted to work in the high-bay racking in Zone B. Counterbalance forklifts, electric pallet jacks and hand pallet jacks never place or retrieve pallets at height in the high bays.

9. No person climbs on racking, stands on pallets or forks, or walks under a raised load. Forks are inserted fully and centrally, loads are tilted slightly back for travel, and pallets are seated squarely on both beams without striking uprights or beams.

10. Any strike, scrape or visible damage to uprights, beams, bracing, base plates, floor fixings or beam locks is reported at once to the shift supervisor in charge of the floor and to the maintenance technician. The affected bay is unloaded if unsafe and is not reloaded until inspected and released.

11. Damaged pallets, rack components, leaning stacks or fallen goods are cordoned off immediately. Loose material is not pulled from the bottom of a stack, and collapsed or unstable stacks are rebuilt only by authorised operators with suitable equipment.

12. Racking is subject to a documented safety inspection every month, logged by the maintenance technician. Defects found between inspections are tagged, reported and repaired, and every repair is recorded in the maintenance log.

13. Put-away to storage follows procedure PR-02 Put-away to storage together with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts. Weight limits, bay labels and stack markings are never altered, removed or ignored.

14. Any overload, bay-limit breach, unstable stack, rack strike or unauthorised alteration of racking is treated as a safety breach and reported immediately to the shift supervisor for review and to the warehouse manager as accountable for the site.

title: Daily Checks and Maintenance
text:
1. No powered truck starts work until its documented daily check has been completed. The check is done before the first use each day and is recorded in writing with truck number, date, checker name and result.

2. The daily check applies to the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t, and the 8 electric pallet jacks. The 12 hand pallet jacks receive a visual and functional check before first use for damage, wheels, forks and handle operation.

3. The check covers brakes, steering, horn, lights, forks, chains, tyres, battery charge and seat belt, plus safety devices, warning beacon and reverse alarm where fitted. For electric pallet jacks it also covers emergency stop, tiller control, lifting and lowering, and charger cable condition.

4. Only authorised forklift operators carry out daily checks on counterbalance forklifts, reach trucks and electric pallet jacks. The check is done in the marked parking position with forks lowered, brake applied and power off before start-up, then a short static and slow-moving test.

5. If any defect is found, the truck is taken out of service immediately, tagged as defective, keys or access devices removed, and reported to the shift supervisor in charge of the floor and to the maintenance technician. No continued use or makeshift repair is permitted.

6. A defective truck returns to service only after repair by or under the direction of the maintenance technician and a recorded re-check. Every repair is logged by the maintenance technician with date, fault, action taken and release signature.

7. Battery charging is done only in the designated charging area with ventilation, charger matched to the truck, cables clear of aisles and walkways, and no smoking or open flame. Damaged connectors, leaking batteries or overheating chargers are reported at once and taken out of use.

8. Each of the 8 dock levellers is checked before its first use each shift for correct seating, lip operation, deck movement, oil leaks, unusual noise, controls and markings. A leveller with gap, bounce, leak or faulty lip is taken out of use and reported.

9. Only trained, authorised staff operate dock levellers, stretch wrappers and the cardboard baler. Guards, emergency stops, light curtains and interlocks are checked before use and never bypassed, removed or disabled.

10. The 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers and the 1 cardboard baler are kept clear of wrap, cardboard dust and waste, and their rollers, turntables and press chambers are inspected daily for damage and obstruction. Faults are tagged and reported for logging.

11. Racking in Zone B receives a documented safety inspection every month, logged by the maintenance technician. Uprights, beams, bracing, base plates, fixings, beam locks and bay load labels are checked, and damaged bays are unloaded if unsafe until inspected and released.

12. Defects found between inspections, including any rack strike, barrier strike, damaged pallet, dock door, bumper, fence, marking, light or yellow pedestrian barrier, are reported at once to the shift supervisor and to the maintenance technician for repair and logging.

13. The 20 handheld WMS scanners and other daily-use aids are checked for damage and function at shift start. Damaged equipment is withdrawn, reported and not used for lifting, securing or propping loads.

14. All checks and maintenance follow procedure PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation together with PR-02 Put-away to storage and PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Check sheets, defect tags and the maintenance log are handed over each shift, and outstanding defects are carried forward until closed.

title: Working in the Cold Zone
text:
1. Zone E is a 300 m2 chilled store held between +2 °C and +8 °C. No goods are stored, picked or staged in Zone E unless they require chilled storage, and no ambient product is placed there to free space elsewhere.

2. Entry to Zone E is limited to assigned tasks only: put-away of booked chilled goods, replenishment to pick faces, picking against a scanner task, cycle counts, and temperature verification. No person loiters, takes shortcuts, or waits in the cold zone.

3. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear remain mandatory inside Zone E with no exception. Additional warm, dry clothing and gloves are worn as under-layers, and the vest is worn outermost and closed so reflective bands stay visible.

4. The cold zone temperature is held by automatic control with audible and visual alarms. Staff respond to any alarm at once, notify the shift supervisor in charge of the floor, and do not continue normal put-away or picking until the supervisor confirms the action.

5. A manual temperature verification is carried out in Zone E in every shift, morning 06:00-14:00 and afternoon 14:00-22:00, and during any Saturday overtime shift. The reading, time, checker name and device used are recorded in writing.

6. The manual check uses a calibrated thermometer at the designated measuring point, with doors closed and after stabilisation. If the reading is outside +2 °C to +8 °C, the checker re-checks, informs the shift supervisor immediately, and quarantines decision on affected stock until reviewed.

7. Doors to Zone E are kept closed except for the immediate passage of goods and personnel. Doors are never wedged open, and curtains, seals and door closers are left to operate. Faulty doors, seals, curtains or icing are reported at once.

8. Only authorised forklift operators drive powered trucks into Zone E, and only after the documented daily check. Condensation on floors, pallets and forks is expected: drivers travel at walking pace, well below the 10 km/h indoor limit, brake gently, and keep forks low with loads tilted slightly back.

9. Pedestrians in Zone E use only marked walkways and crossings, stay clear of moving trucks in the confined chilled area, and make eye contact before crossing. Floors are checked for ice, water and fallen packaging before work starts.

10. Pallets in Zone E meet the site-wide 1,000 kg maximum per pallet and must be intact, stable and wrapped against moisture. Damaged, thawed, leaking or temperature-abused goods are not put to bulk or pick faces and are moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day.

11. Time in the cold is kept as short as the task allows. Staff who feel numbness, shivering, dizziness or loss of grip leave Zone E at once, warm up outside, and report to the shift supervisor. No person works alone in Zone E with the door closed without the supervisor knowing.

12. No eating, drinking or storage of personal food and drink is permitted in Zone E. Spillages, debris and ice build-up are cleaned immediately with suitable non-slip means, and cleaning does not leave standing water to refreeze.

13. Lighting, alarms, thermometers, rack labels and floor markings in Zone E are checked as part of each shift verification. Defects to refrigeration, alarms, doors, racking, levellers serving chilled moves or WMS scanners are reported to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician for logging and repair.

14. All cold-zone work follows procedure PR-12 Cold-chain handling together with PR-02 Put-away to storage, PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces, PR-04 Order picking and PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Temperature records, alarms and any breach are handed over under PR-15 End-of-shift handover and reviewed by the shift supervisor.

title: Hazmat Storage Limits
text:
1. All hazardous goods on site are stored only inside the separate ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F. No hazmat is stored, staged, picked or left temporarily in Zones A, B, C, D or E, in quarantine, on dock staging areas, or in the yard.

2. The hazmat cage is a marked, lockable area of 60 m2 with mechanical ventilation, kept clear and closed except for immediate put-away or removal. Ventilation is left running at all times and is never switched off, blocked or used for drying goods or equipment.

3. The total quantity of hazmat in the cage at any one time must never exceed 4,000 kg, including goods, inner packaging and pallets. The limit applies to the combined weight of everything inside the cage, not per bay or per pallet.

4. A single pallet including its load may weigh at most 1,000 kg. At full pallet weight this means at most 4 pallets in the cage at once. Lighter pallets do not increase the pallet count beyond safe stacking and floor marking, and the 4,000 kg total is never exceeded.

5. Only booked, inspected, correctly labelled and sealed hazmat is put into the cage. Unlabelled containers, open or leaking units, damaged drums or goods without safety documentation are not placed in the cage and are moved to quarantine for decision the same day.

6. Pallets in the cage are intact, stable and within the pallet footprint, and respect the site-wide stacking rules. Free stacking is limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m total height, and unstable, leaning or overhanging pallets are not stored until re-wrapped or re-palletised.

7. Food, drugstore and household goods without hazard classification are never placed inside the cage, even for a short stop. Cold-chain goods are never placed in the cage and remain in Zone E between +2 °C and +8 °C.

8. Only authorised forklift operators move hazmat pallets, using trucks with a documented daily check completed. Hand pallet jacks are not used for cage put-away at height, and forks are kept low with loads tilted slightly back during travel in Zone F.

9. Pedestrian access to the cage is limited to assigned put-away, stock check and emergency tasks. The cage door is kept closed and locked when not in active use, and no person works alone inside the closed cage without the shift supervisor knowing.

10. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for all work at the cage with no exception. Smoking, open flame, battery charging and eating or drinking are prohibited in and directly around the 60 m2 cage area.

11. Incompatible hazard classes are segregated inside the cage by marked positions and never stacked together or against the mesh. Spill kits, fire equipment and safety data are kept accessible outside the cage door and never blocked by pallets or packing material.

12. The cage is checked each shift for weight total, pallet count, labelling, leaks, damage, ventilation operation and clear access. The checker records the quantity on hand against the 4,000 kg limit and reports any over-limit, misplaced or unlabelled stock at once to the shift supervisor.

13. Any leak, damaged container, failed ventilation, missing label or quantity breach stops further put-away to the cage until reviewed. Affected goods are isolated, the area is cordoned off, and spill and damaged-goods action starts immediately under quarantine rules.

14. All hazmat storage follows procedure PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response together with PR-02 Put-away to storage, PR-09 Damaged-goods handling and PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Quantities, checks and any breach are handed over under PR-15 End-of-shift handover and reviewed by the shift supervisor in charge of the floor.

title: Spills and Damaged Goods
text:
1. Any spill, leak or damaged container is acted on immediately where it is found. Work in the affected area stops, the area is cordoned off, and further put-away, picking or truck movement through the spill is prohibited until cleared.

2. The person discovering the spill alerts nearby staff, notifies the shift supervisor in charge of the floor at once, and stays clear upwind where fumes are present. No person touches, tastes, wipes up or moves spilt hazardous material with bare hands.

3. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear remain mandatory during spill response with no exception. Chemical-resistant gloves, eye protection and any equipment stated in the safety data are worn before approaching the spill, with the vest worn outermost.

4. Ventilation in the 60 m2 hazmat cage in Zone F is left running during any hazmat spill and is never switched off. Ignition sources are removed from the cage area: no smoking, no open flame, no battery charging and no electrical switching near flammable spillages.

5. Small contained spillages are absorbed only with the spill kit kept accessible outside the cage door or at the designated Zone F point. Spill kits, fire equipment, safety data and cage access are never blocked by pallets, wrap or packing material.

6. Used absorbents, contaminated packaging and broken containers are placed in sealed, labelled salvage containers and moved to quarantine. They are never placed back in the hazmat cage, in Zone B racking, in Zone C pick faces, or in general waste or the cardboard baler.

7. Leaks in Zone E cold store between +2 °C and +8 °C are treated as temperature-abuse as well as damage. Thawed, leaking or warmed chilled goods are not returned to bulk or pick faces and are moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found.

8. All damaged goods found anywhere on site — in Zone A receiving, Zone B storage, Zone C picking, Zone D dispatch, Zone E or the cage — are moved to the quarantine area in Zone F the same day they are found, intact labelling retained where possible.

9. Quarantined goods are clearly tagged with date, zone found, description, quantity, pallet weight and finder name, and are physically segregated from saleable stock, returns awaiting inspection and hazmat. Only inspected goods are booked into the system.

10. Returns are inspected unit by unit in Zone F within the 14-day acceptance period, and damaged returns go directly to quarantine. Returns staff propose restock, rework or scrap, but no restock is made until inspection is complete and recorded.

11. No quarantined or damaged goods are sold, picked, wrapped for dispatch or placed in the 4,000 kg hazmat total until a disposition decision is recorded. Unlabelled, open or leaking hazmat is never returned to the cage.

12. Disposition follows procedure PR-09 Damaged-goods handling together with PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response and PR-07 Returns handling. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR and the final disposition of inspected returns; any write-off above 500 EUR is signed off only by the warehouse manager.

13. Every spill and every damaged-goods finding is recorded in writing the same day with time, place, product, quantity, action taken and names involved. The report is reviewed by the shift supervisor as part of incident review and handed over under PR-15 End-of-shift handover.

14. After clean-up, the floor is left dry, non-slip and free of ice, water and packaging. Defective containers, failed ventilation, blocked spill kits, faulty lighting or contaminated racking, pallets and scanners are reported to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician for repair and logging before work resumes.

title: Incident Reporting
text:
1. Every injury, near miss, rack or barrier strike, spill, damaged-goods finding, vehicle or equipment defect, and breach of safety rules is treated as an incident and is reported immediately to the shift supervisor in charge of the floor.

2. The person involved or discovering the incident stops unsafe work, makes the area safe where possible without personal risk, alerts nearby staff, and notifies the shift supervisor at once by the fastest means available.

3. Where a person is injured, first aid is given immediately and emergency services are called where needed. The injured area is kept clear, and nothing is moved except to protect life until the shift supervisor confirms the action.

4. The shift supervisor takes charge of incident response on the shift, secures the scene, arranges cover for the floor, and decides whether work in the affected zone may continue. The warehouse manager as accountable for the site is informed without delay of serious injuries and major damage.

5. Near misses are reported in the same way as injuries, including trucks passing too close to pedestrians, loads slipping, pallets striking uprights, barrier contacts at walkways and crossings, and trailer or leveller faults at doors 1-8.

6. Any defect to trucks, racking, dock doors, levellers, barriers, lighting, alarms or WMS equipment found during an incident is tagged out of use where unsafe and reported to the maintenance technician for repair and logging.

7. Every incident is recorded in writing on the same shift with date, time, zone, persons and equipment involved, description of what happened, immediate action taken and witness names. Reports use plain facts and never admit liability or blame.

8. The written report is handed to the shift supervisor for review before end of shift under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Outstanding reports are never left for the next shift without supervisor knowledge and are carried forward until closed.

9. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report, checks completeness, adds follow-up actions, and confirms handover to the next shift and to the warehouse manager. Morning 06:00-14:00, afternoon 14:00-22:00 and any Saturday overtime incidents are each reviewed by the supervisor on duty.

10. Incidents involving damaged goods, spills or returns in Zone F are linked to quarantine tagging under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling and PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response, with date, zone found, quantity and finder name recorded.

11. Incidents involving forklifts, reach trucks, pallet jacks, levellers, wrappers or the baler are handled under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Authorisation, speed, seat-belt and daily-check breaches are stated explicitly in the report.

12. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear remain mandatory during incident response and scene protection, with no exception. Additional protection stated in safety data is worn for spills before approaching the area.

13. No person re-enters a cordoned area, restarts a tagged truck or leveller, or reloads a damaged rack bay until the shift supervisor and, where needed, the maintenance technician release it after inspection and logging.

14. All incident reporting follows PR-15 End-of-shift handover together with the applicable procedure from PR-01 to PR-14. Repeated near misses, barrier strikes and walkway breaches are reviewed for corrective action by the shift supervisor and the warehouse manager as accountable for safety.

title: Evacuation and Re-entry
text:
1. On hearing the evacuation alarm or on instruction from the shift supervisor in charge of the floor, all work stops immediately in every zone. Staff leave goods, scanners and paperwork where they are and evacuate without delay under procedure PR-14 Emergency evacuation.

2. The shift supervisor takes charge of the evacuation on the shift. The supervisor orders the stop, directs movement to exits, prevents re-entry, conducts the roll call and liaises with emergency services. The warehouse manager as accountable for the site is informed as soon as possible.

3. All powered trucks are stopped safely where they will not block walkways, crossings or exits. Forks are lowered, brakes applied, power switched off and keys left secured. Trucks are never driven to exits during an evacuation.

4. Dock levellers, the 2 stretch wrappers and the cardboard baler are left in a safe stopped state where time allows without personal risk. No person delays leaving to finish wrapping, loading, charging batteries or closing paperwork.

5. Everyone leaves the 6,000 m2 hall by the nearest safe marked exit using the 1.2 m pedestrian walkways and marked lanes. Walkways, crossings, stairways and exits are kept clear at all times so evacuation routes are never blocked by pallets, jacks or waste.
