6. Running is prohibited during evacuation to avoid falls on ramps, crossings and dock areas. Staff walk briskly, keep to the right on walkways, give way at crossings, and keep clear of moving emergency vehicles in the yard.

7. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear remain worn during evacuation with no exception. No person stops to change clothing, collect personal items, or return for scanners, keys or documents.

8. Inbound operators, pickers, stock controllers, returns staff, maintenance staff, dispatchers and floaters evacuate from their zone of work. No person uses lifts, climbs racking, crosses truck aisles as a shortcut, or re-enters Zone B high bays, Zone E cold store or the Zone F hazmat cage.

9. Staff in Zone E leave by the cold-store doors and do not stop to check temperatures. Staff in Zone F leave the ventilated hazmat cage area immediately, leaving ventilation running, and do not stop for spills, quarantine goods or returns.

10. Escorted visitors, contractors and drivers under supervision are escorted to the exit by the staff member responsible for them. Drivers in the marked waiting area in the yard move directly to the assembly point and do not enter the hall or approach docks 1-8.

11. The assembly point is by the north fence in the yard. All staff, visitors and drivers present assemble there by shift and team, clear of dock traffic, yard lanes and emergency access. No person waits in the building, on dock ramps or in vehicles.

12. Roll call is conducted at the assembly point before anyone re-enters the building. The shift supervisor checks morning 06:00-14:00, afternoon 14:00-22:00 and any Saturday overtime staff present, plus visitors and drivers notified by the dispatcher, against expected numbers.

13. Missing, injured or unaccounted persons are reported to emergency services at once with last known zone. No person leaves the assembly point or re-enters to search except under direction of emergency services and the shift supervisor.

14. Re-entry is permitted only after the shift supervisor confirms the building is released and conducts a second roll call on return. No work restarts until zones, racking, levellers, alarms and exits are checked, defects are reported to the maintenance technician for logging, and handover is recorded under PR-15 End-of-shift handover.

15. Every evacuation, including each quarterly evacuation drill, is recorded with date, time, zones evacuated, roll-call result and lessons found. Damaged barriers, faded markings, defective alarms, lighting or doors found during evacuation are reported to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician.

title: Safety Roles and Handover
text:
1. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site, including operations, safety and final sign-offs. Nothing overrules that accountability, and where any instruction conflicts with safe operation, the manager's decision applies.

2. The warehouse manager personally authorises every new forklift operator, signs off the annual wall-to-wall stocktake results, approves any damaged-goods write-off above 500 EUR, and is the only person who may approve overtime, including Saturday morning overtime.

3. Each shift is run by the shift supervisor in charge of the floor. The supervisor directs floor staff, controls work in the zones, takes charge of incident response, evacuation and roll call, and decides when a cordoned area, tagged truck or damaged bay may return to use.

4. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report before end of shift, approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR, approves the final disposition of inspected returns into restock, rework or scrap, and ensures handover under PR-15 End-of-shift handover is complete.

5. Dispatchers own dock scheduling. They assign every carrier a door and time slot, keep doors 1-4 inbound only and doors 5-8 outbound only, call drivers forward from the marked waiting area, and release outbound loads only when wrapped, labelled and staged.

6. Forklift operators drive the 6 counterbalance forklifts, 4 reach trucks and 8 electric pallet jacks after documented daily checks. Inbound operators unload, count and inspect in Zone A, pickers pick against scanner tasks in Zone C, and stock controllers own cycle counts, recounts and adjustments.

7. Returns and packing staff inspect returns in Zone F and move damaged goods to quarantine the same day. The maintenance technician maintains trucks, racking, levellers and alarms and logs every repair. Floaters cover absence only as directed by the supervisor.

8. No person performs a task outside their role and authorisation. Without a current licence and personal authorisation from the warehouse manager, no truck of any kind is driven, and only trained, authorised staff operate levellers, stretch wrappers and the cardboard baler.

9. Every shift ends with a documented handover under PR-15. The outgoing shift supervisor hands over to the incoming supervisor, covering staff present, overtime cover, zones in use, dock slots, and any carry-over work in Zones A to F.

10. The handover always includes incidents and near misses, open incident reports, cordoned areas, tagged trucks, defective levellers, rack damage, barrier strikes, spill clean-up status, and quarantine goods with date, zone found, quantity and finder name.

11. Operational handover includes inbound trucks unloaded and awaiting paperwork check, put-away backlogs, pick-face replenishment, outbound staging in Zone D, returns awaiting inspection, cycle-count results and any second count or adjustment pending, and temperature records for Zone E.

12. Handover covers morning 06:00-14:00 to afternoon 14:00-22:00, afternoon to next morning, and any Saturday overtime shift. Outstanding defects and reports are never left without supervisor knowledge and are carried forward in writing until closed by repair and logging.

13. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear remain mandatory during handover walks on the floor and in the yard, seat belts stay fastened on any moving truck, and walkways, crossings and exits are used with no shortcuts through truck aisles or high bays.

14. All roles and handovers follow PR-15 End-of-shift handover together with PR-01 to PR-14 as applicable. Any gap in cover, missing report, unlogged repair or breach of authorisation, speed, PPE or limit rules is reported at once to the shift supervisor and to the warehouse manager as accountable for safety.

title: Warehouse Manager
text:
1. The Warehouse Manager is accountable for the whole Harborwick 3PL site at Port Sellow — all operations, safety, inventory integrity and service to the approximately twenty regular clients.
2. The role covers the single-storey 6,000 m2 hall, the office annex and the 3,500 m2 fenced yard with 8 dock doors, operated Monday to Friday on two shifts, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season.
3. The Warehouse Manager reports to the company owner as site lead and directly manages 2 Shift Supervisors, 2 Dispatchers, 2 Stock Controllers, 1 Maintenance Technician and, through the supervisors, all floor staff of about 38-40 persons in total.
4. The Manager is accountable that stock in the system is stock on the rack for packed food, drugstore and household goods across Zones A to F, including bulk storage, picking, dispatch, cold zone and services.
5. The Manager owns the fifteen written procedures PR-01 to PR-15 and ensures that work is performed in accordance with them; where the manual differs from the owner's brief, the brief prevails.
6. The Manager sets shift cover and ensures one Shift Supervisor is in charge of the floor on every shift to run floor staff and incident response.
7. The Manager ensures that documents are checked before unloading in Zone A, that only inspected goods are booked into the system, and that only booked goods are put away to Zone B, E or F.
8. The Manager ensures pick faces in Zone C are replenished before each picking shift, that picking is scan-verified, and that only wrapped and labelled pallets are staged in Zone D for outbound doors 5-8.
9. The Manager is responsible for observance of site limits: 1,000 kg maximum per pallet including load, 2,700 kg per rack bay, 2,400 pallet positions in Zone B, block stacking to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m, 4,000 kg and 4 full-weight pallets maximum in the 60 m2 hazmat cage, and 288 full-weight pallets per shift maximum outbound capacity.
10. The Manager is responsible for fleet and facility readiness: 6 counterbalance forklifts of 2.5 t, 4 reach trucks of 1.6 t, 8 electric pallet jacks, 12 hand pallet jacks, 2 stretch wrappers, 1 baler, 8 dock levellers and 20 WMS scanners, with a documented check of each truck before first use each day.
11. The Manager enforces mandatory controls: high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear for everyone on the floor, seat belts for forklift operators when moving, speed limits of 10 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h in pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps, and 1.2 m walkways separated by yellow barriers.
12. The Manager ensures the cold zone between +2 C and +8 C with alarms and manual verification each shift, that hazmat sits only in the ventilated cage, that damaged goods go to quarantine the same day, and that returns are accepted within 14 days and inspected in Zone F.
13. The Manager owns the counting regime: cycle counts every working day on rotation with no adjustment without a second count, and a yearly wall-to-wall stocktake under shutdown, plus monthly documented racking inspection and quarterly evacuation drill with roll call at the north fence assembly point.
14. Only the Warehouse Manager authorises new forklift operators under PR-10; no licence, no truck.
15. Only the Warehouse Manager approves overtime.
16. Final sign-offs reserved to the Warehouse Manager are: the yearly stocktake results, any damaged-goods write-off above 500 EUR, and overall release of policy under PR-01 to PR-15.
17. Write-offs up to 500 EUR, final disposition of inspected returns, review of every incident report, and dock scheduling remain with the Shift Supervisor and Dispatcher as defined; the Manager retains oversight and audit right.
18. The Manager reviews incidents, audits compliance, and stops any operation that is unsafe or risks inventory accuracy until corrected.

title: Shift Supervisors
text:
1. The Shift Supervisors run the warehouse floor shift by shift and are accountable to the Warehouse Manager for safe, accurate and on-plan execution during their hours in charge.
2. There are 2 Shift Supervisors covering the two Monday to Friday shifts, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season; one Shift Supervisor is in charge of the floor on every operating shift.
3. Each Shift Supervisor directs the floor staff on shift — inbound operators, pickers, forklift operators, returns and packing staff, stock controllers on count duty, dispatcher on duty and floaters — and coordinates with the Maintenance Technician when equipment or racking needs attention.
4. The Shift Supervisor assigns work, balances labour across Zones A to F against inbound arrivals, replenishment, picking waves and outbound deadlines, and ensures handover to the next shift under PR-15 with open tasks, incidents and equipment status recorded.
5. The Supervisor enforces the goods-flow discipline on shift: documents checked in Zone A before unloading under PR-01, only inspected goods booked, only booked goods put away to Zone B, E or F under PR-02, pick faces in Zone C replenished before each picking shift under PR-03, and only wrapped and labelled pallets staged in Zone D under PR-05 and PR-06.
6. The Supervisor oversees inbound doors 1-4 and outbound doors 5-8 as scheduled by the Dispatcher, keeps drivers in the marked waiting area and out of the hall, and prevents congestion at levellers, staging areas and main transport aisles.
7. The Supervisor enforces site limits on shift: 1,000 kg maximum per pallet including load, 2,700 kg per rack bay, block stacking to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m, hazmat only in the 60 m2 ventilated cage in Zone F up to 4,000 kg, and cold storage in Zone E held between +2 C and +8 C.
8. The Supervisor ensures the manual temperature verification in Zone E is done each shift under PR-12, that alarms and deviations are escalated immediately, and that cold-chain goods are not left unprotected on the floor.
9. The Supervisor enforces mandatory safety controls: high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear for everyone on the floor, seat belts for forklift operators when moving, speed limits of 10 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h in pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps, and use of the 1.2 m walkways separated by yellow barriers.
10. The Supervisor ensures only authorised and licensed operators use trucks under PR-10, that each truck has its documented check before first use each day, and that any defective forklift, reach truck, pallet jack, wrapper, baler, leveller or WMS scanner is tagged out and reported to maintenance.
11. The Supervisor leads immediate incident response on shift under PR-11, PR-13 and PR-14, secures people and stock, calls emergency services where needed, preserves the scene for review, and ensures roll call at the north fence assembly point before anyone re-enters during evacuation.
12. The Supervisor reviews every incident report arising on the shift for completeness and corrective action, and escalates serious safety, food-safety, cold-chain, hazmat or inventory-integrity events to the Warehouse Manager without delay.
13. The Supervisor ensures damaged goods found on shift go to quarantine the same day under PR-09, and that returns inspected in Zone F under PR-07 receive a timely decision on restock, rework or scrap.
14. Delegated approvals held by the Shift Supervisor in charge are: damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR, and final disposition of inspected returns into restock, rework or scrap; write-offs above 500 EUR and the yearly stocktake results are reserved to the Warehouse Manager.
15. The Supervisor supports the counting regime on shift: cycle counts every working day on rotation under PR-08, no adjustment without a second count, and full cooperation with the yearly wall-to-wall stocktake under shutdown.
16. The Supervisor stops any operation that is unsafe or risks inventory accuracy until corrected, and refers overtime needs, new forklift authorisations and policy exceptions to the Warehouse Manager, who alone approves them.

title: Dispatchers
text:
1. The Dispatchers own dock scheduling and outbound load release at Harborwick 3PL and are accountable to the Warehouse Manager for on-time, accurate and safe transport execution.
2. There are 2 Dispatchers covering the Monday to Friday two-shift operation, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season, working in close coordination with the Shift Supervisor in charge of the floor.
3. The Dispatchers book all inbound and outbound transport, confirm carrier, trailer or van type, quantities and time slots in advance, and refuse unscheduled arrivals without a slot.
4. The Dispatcher assigns every carrier a specific dock door and time slot: doors 1-4 are inbound only for Zone A receiving, doors 5-8 are outbound only for Zone D dispatch, with no interchange.
5. Drivers wait only in the marked waiting area outside the hall and never enter the warehouse floor; the Dispatcher and Shift Supervisor enforce this separation on every load.
6. The Dispatchers plan within proven site capacity: 4 outbound doors each handling 3 trailer loads per shift, making 288 full-weight pallets per shift the most that can be promised to clients.
7. Booking respects load limits built on the 1,000 kg maximum per pallet including load: contracted curtain-side trailers carry 24,000 kg on 33 floor positions, equating to 24 full-weight pallets, while the delivery van carries 1,200 kg on 6 positions for one full-weight pallet, with anything heavier routed by trailer.
8. The Dispatchers sequence inbound arrivals to Zone A so that documents are checked before anything is unloaded under PR-01, and only inspected and booked goods are released for put-away to Zone B, E or F under PR-02.
9. The Dispatchers sequence outbound work to Zone D under PR-06 so that picking in Zone C, packing and labelling under PR-04 and PR-05, wrapping on the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers, and staging are complete before the truck is called to the door.
10. Only wrapped and labelled pallets are staged in Zone D in front of docks 5-8; the Dispatcher verifies load, destination, labels and WMS status before release.
11. The Dispatcher formally releases each outbound load, authorises loading via dock leveller at the assigned door, and ensures the truck is loaded, counted and sealed as documented.
12. The Dispatchers maintain the dock plan, leveller availability, staging discipline and yard flow, preventing congestion at doors, main 4.0 m transport aisles and dock ramps, and escalating delays or no-shows to the Shift Supervisor and Warehouse Manager.
13. The Dispatchers enforce driver and yard safety rules for movements under their control: 15 km/h in the 3,500 m2 yard, 10 km/h inside, 5 km/h in pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps, use of 1.2 m walkways separated by yellow barriers, and high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear for anyone entering the floor.
14. Cold-chain loads from Zone E between +2 C and +8 C and hazmat loads from the 60 m2 ventilated cage in Zone F up to 4,000 kg are released only when PR-12 and PR-13 conditions are met, with no hazmat staged outside the cage.
15. The Dispatchers record every booking, arrival, departure, seal number and exception in the WMS, hand over open loads, pending carriers and door status to the next shift under PR-15, and support cycle counts and the yearly wall-to-wall stocktake so system stock remains stock on the rack.
16. The Dispatchers stop any loading that is unsafe, overweight, unwrapped, unlabelled or unreleased, refer overtime needs, policy exceptions and new carrier approvals to the Warehouse Manager, and retain no write-off or stock-adjustment authority.

title: Inbound Operators
text:
1. The Inbound Operators are responsible for unloading, counting and inspection of all incoming goods in Zone A receiving and are accountable to the Shift Supervisor in charge of the floor for accuracy and discipline at receipt.
2. There are 6 Inbound Operators covering the Monday to Friday two-shift operation, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season when approved by the Warehouse Manager.
3. Inbound Operators work only in the 800 m2 Zone A receiving area at inbound docks 1-4, with unloading, staging for inspection and handover for put-away to Zone B, E or F; they do not stage goods in Zone C picking or Zone D dispatch.
4. No truck is unloaded until paperwork is checked under PR-01; the Inbound Operator verifies carrier, dock door and time slot as assigned by the Dispatcher, checks delivery documents against the booking, and holds any unscheduled arrival or document mismatch for the Shift Supervisor.
5. Drivers remain in the marked waiting area and never enter the hall; Inbound Operators do not bring drivers onto the floor and enforce separation at doors 1-4 and dock levellers.
6. Unloading is performed safely via dock leveller at the assigned door, respecting the 1,000 kg maximum per pallet including load, the 24,000 kg and 33-position limit of curtain-side trailers, and the 5 km/h limit at dock ramps, crossings and pedestrian zones.
7. After unloading, Inbound Operators count every pallet, carton and unit as required, compare quantity to documents and WMS expectation, and record overages, shortages and visible damage immediately in the WMS scanner before any booking.
8. Only inspected goods are booked into the system under PR-01, and only booked goods go to put-away under PR-02; nothing moves past Zone A to bulk storage in Zone B, cold storage in Zone E or the services area in Zone F until inspection and booking are complete.
9. Inspection covers packaging integrity, labelling, expiry and batch where applicable, temperature condition for chilled goods, and hazmat marking; cold-chain goods for Zone E between +2 C and +8 C are prioritised for rapid transfer under PR-12, and hazmat is passed only to the 60 m2 ventilated cage in Zone F under PR-13 up to 4,000 kg.
10. Any damaged, suspect or non-conforming goods found at receipt go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09, with WMS status, labels and location correctly applied; Inbound Operators post no stock adjustment and approve no write-off.
11. Inbound Operators prepare clean pallets for put-away by the Forklift Operators, keep inspection lanes clear, respect the 4.0 m main transport aisles and 3.0 m rack aisles where they interface with Zone B, and never exceed block-stacking of 3 pallets high and 4.0 m or the 2,700 kg per rack bay limit in staging.
12. Small moves are made with hand pallet jacks and electric pallet jacks where authorised; counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t and reach trucks rated at 1.6 t are operated only by authorised Forklift Operators under PR-10 after documented daily check, and Inbound Operators tag out and report any defective truck, leveller or WMS scanner.
13. Mandatory controls apply at all times: high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear on the floor, 10 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the yard, 5 km/h where people and trucks meet, and use of the 1.2 m walkways separated by yellow barriers under PR-11.
14. Inbound Operators use the 20 shared handheld WMS scanners for receipt, count and inspection transactions, ensuring system stock remains stock on the rack, and support cycle counts under PR-08 and the yearly wall-to-wall stocktake as directed.
15. Inbound Operators hand over open vehicles, pending inspections, quarantine moves and equipment faults to the next shift under PR-15, cooperate with Stock Controllers on recounts, and escalate incidents, spills, cold-chain deviations and repeat supplier errors to the Shift Supervisor without delay.
16. Inbound Operators stop any receipt that is unsafe, undocumented, overweight or temperature-compromised until corrected, and refer overtime, door changes and policy exceptions to the Shift Supervisor and Warehouse Manager.

title: Pickers
text:
1. The Pickers are responsible for scanner-directed picking of customer orders in Zone C and are accountable to the Shift Supervisor in charge of the floor for pick accuracy, verification discipline and on-time transfer to dispatch.
2. There are 10 Pickers covering the Monday to Friday two-shift operation, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season when approved by the Warehouse Manager.
3. Pickers work only in the 1,200 m2 Zone C picking area at ground-level pick faces and flow racks fed from bulk storage in Zone B; they do not pick from high-bay racking, Zone E, or the hazmat cage in Zone F.
4. Pick faces are replenished from bulk before each picking shift under PR-03; Pickers confirm replenishment is complete, report empty or low faces immediately, and never pick from an unreplenished, unlabelled or suspect location.
5. All picking is performed strictly against WMS scanner tasks under PR-04 using the shared 20 handheld scanners; Pickers follow task sequence, location, batch, expiry and quantity prompts, and never pick from memory, paper notes or verbal instruction.
6. Every picked item is scan-verified before it is packed under PR-04 and PR-05; any scan mismatch, short pick, damaged unit or label defect is held, rechecked and escalated to the Shift Supervisor with no system adjustment posted by the Picker.
7. Pickers respect product integrity during picking, including rotation, handling of packed food, drugstore and household goods, and prioritised handling of chilled goods for Zone E between +2 C and +8 C under PR-12 without leaving cold-chain goods unprotected on the floor.
8. Pickers do not handle hazmat picking except as a directed task from the ventilated 60 m2 cage in Zone F under PR-13; hazmat is never staged outside the cage and never above 4,000 kg in total.
9. After verification, Pickers pack, label and consolidate picked goods per PR-05 and move them only to Zone D dispatch staging in front of outbound doors 5-8; only wrapped and labelled pallets are staged in Zone D for release by the Dispatcher under PR-06.
10. Pickers observe load and aisle limits at all times: 1,000 kg maximum per pallet including load, no block stacking above 3 pallets high and 4.0 m in staging, 4.0 m main transport aisles kept clear, and 3.0 m rack storage aisles used without obstruction.
11. Small moves within Zone C and to Zone D are made with hand pallet jacks and electric pallet jacks where authorised; counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t and reach trucks rated at 1.6 t are operated only by authorised Forklift Operators under PR-10, and Pickers tag out and report any defective jack, wrapper or scanner.
12. Mandatory controls apply at all times: high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear on the floor, 10 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the yard, 5 km/h in pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps, and use of the 1.2 m walkways separated by yellow barriers under PR-11.
13. Any damaged goods found during picking go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09, with correct WMS status and labels; Pickers approve no write-off and decide no restock, rework or scrap.
14. Pickers support inventory accuracy as directed: cooperation with daily cycle counts on rotation and the yearly wall-to-wall stocktake under shutdown per PR-08, with no adjustment posted without a second count by Stock Controllers.
15. Pickers hand over open tasks, wave progress, exceptions and equipment faults to the next shift under PR-15, keep pick faces, flow racks and transfer lanes clean and orderly, and escalate incidents, spills, cold-chain deviations and repeat location errors to the Shift Supervisor without delay.
16. Pickers stop any pick that is unsafe, unverified, overweight or temperature-compromised until corrected, and refer overtime, wave changes and policy exceptions to the Shift Supervisor and Warehouse Manager.

title: Forklift Operators
text:
1. The Forklift Operators are responsible for all powered materials-handling movements between Zones A to F and are accountable to the Shift Supervisor in charge of the floor for safe, damage-free and system-accurate transport.
2. There are 8 Forklift Operators covering the Monday to Friday two-shift operation, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season when approved by the Warehouse Manager.
3. Forklift Operators operate the site fleet under PR-10: 6 electric counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t for general work including docks and Zone D staging, 4 electric reach trucks rated at 1.6 t for high-bay work in Zone B, and 8 electric pallet jacks for low-level transfers; 12 hand pallet jacks are shared for small moves.
4. No licence, no truck: only operators expressly authorised by the Warehouse Manager may drive counterbalance forklifts, reach trucks or electric pallet jacks, and authorisation is task- and truck-type specific with training records held.
5. Every truck receives a documented safety check before its first use each day under PR-10; the Operator completes brakes, steering, lights, horn, forks, chains, battery, tyres and emergency stop, and no defective truck is used.
6. Any defective forklift, reach truck, pallet jack, dock leveller, stretch wrapper or WMS scanner is immediately tagged out, parked clear of aisles and doors, and reported to the Shift Supervisor and Maintenance Technician with the check sheet retained.
7. Forklift Operators perform put-away to Zone B, E or F under PR-02 only for inspected and booked goods, replenishment of Zone C pick faces from bulk under PR-03 before each picking shift, and transfer of wrapped and labelled pallets to Zone D under PR-05 and PR-06; nothing is moved past Zone A before booking.
8. Operators serve inbound docks 1-4 and outbound docks 5-8 as directed by the Dispatcher and Shift Supervisor, work via levellers at the assigned door, and never bring drivers from the marked waiting area into the hall.
9. Speed and separation limits are enforced on every move under PR-11: 10 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the 3,500 m2 yard, and 5 km/h wherever people and trucks meet — marked pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps.
10. Operators give way to pedestrians at all times, use only the 4.0 m main transport aisles and 3.0 m rack storage aisles, keep the 1.2 m walkways separated by yellow barriers clear, and sound horn, reduce speed and stop on blind corners, doorways and cold-zone entries.
11. Mandatory controls apply at all times: high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear on the floor, seat belts fastened whenever the truck is moving, forks lowered when travelling, and no passengers, no raised-load travel and no overhang into pedestrian routes.
12. Load limits are observed on every lift: 1,000 kg maximum per pallet including load, 2,700 kg maximum per rack bay in the 2,400-position high bay in Zone B, free block-stacking to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m only, and cold and hazmat limits as directed.
13. Cold-chain pallets for Zone E held between +2 C and +8 C are moved without delay under PR-12 and never left unprotected on the floor; hazmat moves only to and from the 60 m2 ventilated cage in Zone F under PR-13, never staged elsewhere and never above 4,000 kg total.
14. Operators use the shared 20 handheld WMS scanners for every put-away, replenishment and transfer task, confirm source, destination and pallet identity by scan, and post no inventory adjustment; overages, shortages and damage are reported for Stock Controllers to recount.
15. Any damaged or suspect goods found in handling go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09 with correct status and labels; Operators approve no write-off and decide no restock, rework or scrap.
16. Operators hand over open tasks, battery charge status, truck faults and aisle or rack damage to the next shift under PR-15, support daily cycle counts and the yearly wall-to-wall stocktake under PR-08, and attend evacuation drills with roll call at the north fence assembly point under PR-14.
17. Operators stop any lift that is unsafe, overweight, unstable, unwrapped where required, or at risk to people, stock or racking until corrected, and refer overtime, new authorisations and policy exceptions to the Shift Supervisor and Warehouse Manager.

title: Returns and Packing Staff
text:
1. The Returns and Packing Staff are responsible for returns inspection in Zone F and for value-added packing, labelling and preparation for restock or dispatch, and are accountable to the Shift Supervisor in charge of the floor for thorough inspection and correct proposals.
2. There are 4 Returns and Packing Staff covering the Monday to Friday two-shift operation, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season when approved by the Warehouse Manager.
3. Returns and Packing Staff work only in the 600 m2 Zone F services and control area — value-added packing stations, quarantine, returns inspection and handover points for the separate 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage; they do not receive in Zone A or pick in Zone C.
4. Returns are accepted only within 14 days of delivery under PR-07; staff verify delivery date, client, quantities and reason for return against WMS and documents, and hold late, undocumented or mismatched returns for the Shift Supervisor.
5. Every returned unit is inspected under PR-07 for packaging integrity, labelling, batch, expiry, contamination, temperature exposure and damage; no return is restocked, reworked or scrapped without full inspection and WMS recording via the shared 20 handheld scanners.
6. After inspection, staff propose disposition only — restock, rework or scrap — with reasons, evidence and photographs where required; final disposition of inspected returns is decided by the Shift Supervisor, and damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR are reserved to the Warehouse Manager under PR-09.
7. Goods judged saleable are cleaned, repacked and relabelled under PR-05, re-booked only through Stock Controllers and the system, and passed for put-away to Zone B, Zone E or pick faces by Forklift Operators; nothing is returned to stock without approved disposition and system transaction.
8. Damaged, expired, contaminated or otherwise non-conforming goods go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09, with correct WMS status, labels, segregation and location; Returns and Packing Staff post no stock adjustment and approve no write-off.
9. Value-added packing is performed to client instruction under PR-05 — repacking, kitting, labelling and pallet preparation — with every packed item scan-verified where applicable and only wrapped and labelled pallets forwarded to Zone D for release by the Dispatcher under PR-06.
10. Cold-chain returns for Zone E held between +2 C and +8 C are prioritised for rapid inspection under PR-12 and never left unprotected on the floor; alarms and deviations are escalated immediately to the Shift Supervisor.
11. Hazmat returns are handled only under PR-13 in the ventilated cage, never staged elsewhere and never above 4,000 kg total; Returns and Packing Staff do not store hazmat outside the cage and escalate any leak, spill or marking defect as an incident without delay.
12. Load and storage limits are observed on every pallet handled: 1,000 kg maximum per pallet including load, 2,700 kg per rack bay where interfaced, block stacking to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m only, with 4.0 m main transport aisles and 3.0 m rack aisles kept clear.
13. Small moves within Zone F are made with hand pallet jacks and electric pallet jacks where authorised; the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t and 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t are operated only by authorised Forklift Operators under PR-10, and any defective jack, wrapper, baler, leveller or scanner is tagged out and reported.
14. Mandatory controls apply at all times: high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear on the floor, 10 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the yard, 5 km/h in pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps, and use of the 1.2 m walkways separated by yellow barriers under PR-11.
15. Returns and Packing Staff support inventory accuracy as directed: cooperation with daily cycle counts on rotation and the yearly wall-to-wall stocktake under shutdown per PR-08, with no adjustment posted without a second count, and operation of the 2 stretch wrappers and cardboard baler only as trained.
16. Staff hand over open returns, quarantine holds, packing orders, rework status and equipment faults to the next shift under PR-15, keep Zone F clean, segregated and orderly, and stop any return or packing task that is unsafe, uninspected, overweight or temperature-compromised until corrected.

title: Stock Controllers
text:
1. The Stock Controllers own inventory accuracy day to day at Harborwick 3PL and are accountable to the Warehouse Manager for cycle counts, recounts, adjustments and system-to-rack alignment for packed food, drugstore and household goods.
2. There are 2 Stock Controllers covering the Monday to Friday two-shift operation, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season when approved by the Warehouse Manager, working under the direction of the Shift Supervisor in charge of the floor while on shift.
3. Stock Controllers work across Zones A to F, with principal focus on bulk storage in Zone B with 2,200 m2 and 2,400 pallet positions, pick faces in Zone C of 1,200 m2, dispatch staging in Zone D, cold storage in Zone E and quarantine and services in Zone F.
4. The counting regime under PR-08 is owned by the Stock Controllers: cycle counts run every working day on a rotating zone schedule, and once a year a full wall-to-wall stocktake is executed under shutdown for sign-off by the Warehouse Manager.
5. Daily cycle-count tasks are generated, sequenced and performed via the shared 20 handheld WMS scanners; Stock Controllers verify location, pallet identity, quantity, batch and expiry by scan, and keep system stock as stock on the rack.
6. No adjustment is ever posted without a second count; the Stock Controller who performed the first count does not confirm their own adjustment, and every recount, variance cause and correction is documented in the WMS before posting.
7. Stock Controllers investigate every variance to root cause — receipt error in Zone A, put-away error to Zone B, E or F under PR-02, replenishment error to Zone C under PR-03, picking error under PR-04, packing and dispatch error under PR-05 and PR-06, or returns and quarantine error under PR-07 and PR-09 — and escalate repeat location errors to the Shift Supervisor.
8. Only inspected goods booked under PR-01 may appear in stock; Stock Controllers hold open receipts in Zone A, unbooked pallets and moves past Zone A without booking for correction and prevent their inclusion in count results.
9. Stock Controllers control quarantine and blocked-stock status in Zone F under PR-09 in coordination with Inbound Operators, Pickers, Forklift Operators and Returns and Packing Staff; damaged goods found are moved to quarantine the same day they are found and remain system-blocked until disposition.
10. Stock Controllers process system re-booking of inspected returns proposed for restock under PR-07 only after final disposition by the Shift Supervisor; they post no restock without approved disposition and system transaction, and decide no scrap or rework themselves.
11. Stock Controllers approve no damaged-goods write-off; write-offs up to 500 EUR are approved by the Shift Supervisor and write-offs above 500 EUR and the yearly stocktake results are reserved to the Warehouse Manager, with Stock Controllers providing counts, evidence and WMS history.
12. Site limits are verified during every count: 1,000 kg maximum per pallet including load, 2,700 kg per rack bay, block stacking to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m, cold storage in Zone E held between +2 C and +8 C, and hazmat only in the 60 m2 ventilated cage in Zone F up to 4,000 kg and 4 full-weight pallets.
13. Stock Controllers verify cold-chain and hazmat locations with priority, ensure manual temperature verification each shift under PR-12 is recorded, escalate alarms and deviations immediately, and never count unlabelled or suspect hazmat outside the cage under PR-13.
14. Small moves for counts are made with hand pallet jacks and electric pallet jacks where authorised; the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t and 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t are operated only by authorised Forklift Operators under PR-10, and any defective jack, leveller or scanner is tagged out and reported.
15. Mandatory controls apply at all times: high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear on the floor, 10 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the yard, 5 km/h in pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps, and use of the 1.2 m walkways separated by yellow barriers under PR-11.
16. Stock Controllers hand over count coverage, open variances, pending recounts, blocked locations and equipment faults to the next shift under PR-15, support monthly racking inspection and quarterly evacuation drill with roll call at the north fence assembly point, and stop any count or adjustment that is unsafe, unverified or procedurally non-compliant until corrected.

title: Maintenance Technician
text:
1. The Maintenance Technician is responsible for upkeep of trucks, racking and dock equipment at Harborwick 3PL and is accountable to the Warehouse Manager for equipment safety, availability and complete repair logging.
2. There is 1 Maintenance Technician covering the Monday to Friday two-shift operation, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season when approved by the Warehouse Manager, working to priorities set by the Shift Supervisor in charge of the floor.
3. The Technician maintains the full site across the 6,000 m2 hall, 3,500 m2 yard and Zones A to F: powered fleet, racking, dock doors and levellers, wrappers, baler, scanners and safety installations.
4. Fleet under PR-10 comprises 6 electric counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, 4 electric reach trucks rated at 1.6 t, 8 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks; no other powered trucks are used or maintained.
5. Facility equipment comprises 8 dock levellers at doors 1-4 inbound and 5-8 outbound, 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers in Zone D, 1 cardboard baler in Zone F, 20 handheld WMS scanners, racking with 2,400 positions in Zone B, cold-zone alarms and the ventilated hazmat cage.
6. Every truck receives a documented check before its first use each day under PR-10; the Technician reviews check sheets, follows up defects, and retains records for audit by the Warehouse Manager.
7. Any defective truck, pallet jack, leveller, wrapper, baler or scanner tagged out by operators is secured by the Technician, parked clear of 4.0 m main aisles, 3.0 m rack aisles and doors, and not returned to service until inspected, repaired and signed off.
8. The Technician performs planned and reactive maintenance only as competent and trained, isolates energy sources, uses lock-out and correct parts, and escalates specialist electrical, high-bay racking or cold-plant work to approved contractors via the Warehouse Manager.
9. Racking receives a documented safety inspection every month, covering uprights, beams, fixings, bay loading notices and impact damage in Zone B, Zone C flow racks and Zone E; damage is quarantined, off-loaded where needed and logged until repaired.
10. Site limits are protected during maintenance: 1,000 kg maximum per pallet including load, 2,700 kg per rack bay, block stacking to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m, hazmat only in the 60 m2 cage in Zone F up to 4,000 kg, and cold storage in Zone E held between +2 C and +8 C.
11. The Technician supports cold-chain integrity under PR-12 and hazmat safety under PR-13, maintaining alarms, ventilation, segregation and spill equipment, and responds immediately to alarms, leaks or spills as directed by the Shift Supervisor.
12. Every repair, inspection, adjustment and return to service is logged the same day with date, equipment identity, fault, action, parts and sign-off; logs are available to the Shift Supervisor and Warehouse Manager and support incident review under PR-11 and PR-14.
13. The Technician enforces mandatory controls while working: high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear on the floor, seat belts when operating trucks, 10 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h in pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps, and use of 1.2 m walkways separated by yellow barriers.
14. Only the Warehouse Manager authorises new forklift operators under PR-10; the Technician provides technical assessment and training support but grants no driving authorisation and approves no overtime.
15. The Technician hands over open faults, tagged-out equipment, pending parts, racking holds and contractor visits to the next shift under PR-15, keeps workshop and stores clean and orderly, and supports daily cycle counts and the yearly wall-to-wall stocktake by ensuring scanners and handling equipment are available.
16. The Technician attends quarterly evacuation drills with roll call at the north fence assembly point under PR-14, stops any equipment that is unsafe, overloaded, leaking or electrically suspect until corrected, and refers policy exceptions and write-off or stock decisions to the Shift Supervisor and Warehouse Manager.

title: Common Standards for All Roles
text:
1. These Common Standards apply to every person working at Harborwick 3PL Ltd. in Port Sellow, including the Warehouse Manager, Shift Supervisors, Dispatchers, Inbound Operators, Pickers, Forklift Operators, Returns and Packing Staff, Stock Controllers, Maintenance Technician and Floaters, totalling about 38-40 staff.
2. The Warehouse Manager is accountable for the whole site — operations, safety and inventory integrity — and reports to the company owner; all other roles report to the Warehouse Manager directly or through the Shift Supervisor in charge of the floor.
3. Each shift has one Shift Supervisor in charge of the floor, directing floor staff and incident response; Dispatchers own dock scheduling, Stock Controllers own day-to-day accuracy, and functional leads own their procedures under PR-01 to PR-15.
4. Normal working time is Monday to Friday on two shifts, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season; only the Warehouse Manager approves overtime and no overtime is worked without prior approval.
5. All staff work to the fifteen written procedures PR-01 to PR-15 and to the owner's brief, which prevails if the manual differs; ignorance of procedures is not accepted and deviations are escalated immediately.
6. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor at all times, with no exceptions for visitors, drivers entering controlled areas, or office staff.
7. Forklift operators wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving, with forks lowered when travelling, and no passengers are carried; only operators expressly authorised by the Warehouse Manager may drive trucks under PR-10.
8. Site speed limits are enforced for all movements: 10 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the 3,500 m2 yard, and 5 km/h wherever people and trucks meet, including pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps.
9. Pedestrians use only the 1.2 m walkways physically separated by yellow barriers, give way discipline applies in 4.0 m main transport aisles and 3.0 m rack storage aisles, and drivers wait only in the marked waiting area and never in the hall.
10. Every new starter completes mandatory induction before unsupervised work: site layout across Zones A to F, PR-01 to PR-15 relevant to the role, pedestrian safety under PR-11, emergency evacuation under PR-14, and WMS scanner basics using the 20 shared devices.
11. Role-specific mandatory training is completed and refreshed as directed: goods flow and inspection for handlers, scan-verified picking and packing, cold-chain handling under PR-12, hazmat handling and spill response under PR-13, daily truck checks under PR-10, and cycle-count discipline under PR-08.
12. Evacuation drills are held every quarter with roll call at the assembly point by the north fence before anyone re-enters; racking receives a documented safety inspection every month and every truck receives a documented check before first use each day.
13. Site limits are binding on all roles: 1,000 kg maximum per pallet including load, 2,700 kg per rack bay, block stacking to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m, cold storage between +2 °C and +8 °C, and hazmat only in the 60 m2 ventilated cage up to 4,000 kg.
14. Everyone protects system accuracy so stock in the system is stock on the rack: correct WMS scans, no adjustment without a second count, damaged goods to quarantine the same day, and no write-off or restock authority except as defined for Supervisor and Manager.
15. Every shift closes with handover under PR-15 covering open tasks, vehicles at doors 1-8, incidents, quarantine holds and equipment faults; incident reports are completed promptly and reviewed by the Shift Supervisor in charge.
16. Any person must stop work that is unsafe, overweight, unverified, temperature-compromised or procedurally non-compliant until corrected, and refer overtime, new driving authorisations and policy exceptions to the Shift Supervisor and Warehouse Manager.

title: Receiving Hours, Doors and Intake
text:
1. Receiving services are provided Monday to Friday during the two operating shifts: morning shift 06:00–14:00 and afternoon shift 14:00–22:00. A shift supervisor is in charge of the floor throughout each shift.

2. Saturday receiving is available only as peak-season overtime on Saturday morning. Overtime is approved solely by the warehouse manager and must be agreed with the Client in advance. No regular receiving is promised outside the Monday to Friday shifts.

3. Inbound handling is performed exclusively through Doors 1–4, which are designated inbound only. Doors 5–8 are outbound only and shall not be used for receiving. All inbound doors are 1.2 m dock height with individual dock levellers.

4. All inbound arrivals require a prior time slot and door assignment from the dispatcher. The dispatcher owns dock scheduling. Carriers without a confirmed slot and assigned door will not be unloaded until a slot becomes available.

5. Drivers shall wait in the marked waiting area in the fenced yard. Drivers are not permitted in the hall or in Zone A working areas. This rule applies to every delivery without exception.

6. Receiving, unloading and goods inspection take place in Zone A, the 800 m2 receiving zone serving Doors 1–4. The intake sequence follows written procedure PR-01 Inbound receiving.

7. No goods shall be unloaded before the transport documents are checked. Document check is the mandatory first step for every inbound truck at its assigned door.

8. Nothing moves past Zone A until the paperwork has been checked. Goods that fail document check are held in Zone A and are not booked, not put away, and not moved to Zone B, E or F.

9. After successful document check, Harborwick 3PL unloads, counts and inspects the goods in Zone A. This is performed by inbound operators, with forklift operators supporting mechanical handling using electric equipment as required.

10. Only inspected goods are booked into the warehouse management system. Booking is based on counted and inspected quantities, not on declared quantities on the delivery note.

11. Only booked goods are released for put-away to Zone B bulk storage, Zone E cold zone, or Zone F services and control, in accordance with PR-02 Put-away to storage. Unbooked goods remain in Zone A under control of the inbound team.

12. Put-away respects product requirements identified at inspection. Chilled goods requiring +2 °C to +8 °C are directed to Zone E under PR-12 Cold-chain handling. Goods requiring the ventilated hazmat cage are directed only to the 60 m2 cage in Zone F under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response, subject to the 4,000 kg cage limit.

13. All palletised inbound handling is based on a maximum of 1,000 kg per pallet, load included. Contracted curtain-side trailers are handled as 33 floor positions with up to 24,000 kg total load.

14. Yard and building traffic rules apply to every inbound movement. The speed limit is 15 km/h in the yard, 10 km/h inside the building, and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps. Pedestrian walkways are separated by yellow barriers and are 1.2 m wide.

15. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor during receiving. Forklift seat belts are worn whenever the truck is moving, and no truck is operated without a licence authorised by the warehouse manager and a documented check before first use each day.

title: Dispatch Hours, Capacity and Release
text:
1. Dispatch services are provided Monday to Friday during the two operating shifts: morning shift 06:00–14:00 and afternoon shift 14:00–22:00. A shift supervisor is in charge of the floor throughout each shift.

2. Saturday dispatch is available only as peak-season overtime on Saturday morning. Overtime is approved solely by the warehouse manager and must be agreed with the Client in advance. No regular dispatch is promised outside the Monday to Friday shifts.

3. Outbound handling is performed exclusively through Doors 5–8, which are designated outbound only. Doors 1–4 are inbound only and shall not be used for dispatch. All outbound doors are 1.2 m dock height with individual dock levellers.

4. All outbound collections require a prior time slot and door assignment from the dispatcher. The dispatcher owns dock scheduling, books transport, assigns dock doors and releases outbound loads. Carriers without a confirmed slot and assigned door will not be loaded until a slot becomes available.

5. Drivers shall wait in the marked waiting area in the fenced yard. Drivers are not permitted in the hall or in Zone D working areas. This rule applies to every collection without exception.

6. Dispatch staging takes place in Zone D, the 900 m2 dispatch zone serving Doors 5–8. The dispatch sequence follows written procedure PR-06 Outbound dispatch, supported by PR-05 Packing and labelling and PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.

7. Only wrapped, labelled pallets are admitted to Zone D staging. Pallets are wrapped on the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers, labelled after scan-verified picking and packing in Zone C, and moved to Zone D staged for their assigned outbound door.

8. No load is loaded without release by the dispatcher. Release confirms that the staged pallets, quantities, labels and assigned door and time slot match the outbound order. Unreleased staging remains under control of the dispatch team in Zone D.

9. After release, the truck is loaded at its assigned door and sealed. Loading is performed by forklift operators with electric equipment, observing dock-ramp controls and pedestrian separation under PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse.

10. Committed outbound capacity per shift is 3 trailer loads per outbound door. With 4 outbound doors, this is 12 trailer loads per shift across the site.

11. Pallet capacity is based on a maximum of 1,000 kg per pallet, load included. Each contracted curtain-side trailer carries 33 floor positions up to 24,000 kg total, which is 24 full-weight pallets. Maximum committed throughput is therefore 288 full-weight pallets per shift.

12. Lighter pallets do not increase the trailer count beyond 12 loads per shift or the floor-position limit of 33 positions per trailer. The delivery van, where used, carries 1,200 kg on 6 positions and is limited to one full-weight pallet per trip.

13. End-of-shift handover under PR-15 applies to dispatch. Uncompleted stagings, released but unloaded loads, and door-slot changes are recorded and handed to the next shift supervisor and dispatcher.

14. Yard and building traffic rules apply to every outbound movement. The speed limit is 15 km/h in the yard, 10 km/h inside the building, and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide and pedestrian walkways are separated by yellow barriers and are 1.2 m wide.

15. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor during dispatch. Forklift seat belts are worn whenever the truck is moving, and no truck is operated without a licence authorised by the warehouse manager and a documented check before first use each day.

title: Order Accuracy and Packing
text:
1. Order picking is performed exclusively in Zone C, the 1,200 m2 picking zone with ground-level pick faces and flow racks. All picks are executed against warehouse management system scanner tasks. No picking is performed from bulk storage, receiving, or dispatch zones.

2. Pick faces in Zone C are replenished from Zone B bulk storage before each picking shift. Replenishment follows written procedure PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces and is completed before pickers start scanner tasks for that shift.

3. Replenishment moves are performed by forklift operators using electric counterbalance forklifts, reach trucks, and pallet jacks as appropriate for the location. Only booked stock from Zone B is used for replenishment. Stock requiring chilled or hazmat conditions is replenished only to its designated compliant pick location.

4. Picking follows written procedure PR-04 Order picking. Pickers pick only the quantity and product directed by the active scanner task. Picking without a scanner task, from an unreplenished face, or from an unlabelled location is not permitted.

5. Every picked item is scan-verified before it is packed. The picker scans the product and the pick location with a handheld WMS scanner, and the system must confirm the match before the pick is confirmed. A pick that fails scan verification is not packed and is held for check by the shift supervisor.

6. After successful scan verification, goods are packed under written procedure PR-05 Packing and labelling. Packing is performed in Zone C and Zone F value-added packing areas by pickers and packing staff. Damaged or suspect units found during picking are not packed for dispatch and are transferred to quarantine the same day under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.

7. Every packed unit and pallet is labelled before transfer out of the picking area. Labels identify the Client, order, contents, and outbound destination as required for dispatch release. Unlabelled or mislabelled packs are not admitted to Zone D.

8. Labelled packs are moved to Zone D dispatch staging, where pallets are wrapped on the semi-automatic stretch wrappers and staged for their assigned outbound door. Only wrapped, labelled pallets are staged for loading. Wrapping and staging do not replace scan verification as the accuracy control.

9. Order accuracy is defined as the match between the scanned, labelled and staged order and the Client order released for picking. The control standard is 100% scan verification of picks plus label verification before Zone D transfer. Any order line that was not scan-verified is treated as non-compliant, even if the quantity is subsequently found correct.

10. Short picks, overpicks, and scan mismatches are corrected before staging. The picker alerts the shift supervisor, the pick face stock is rechecked, and the corrected pick is re-scanned from start. No manual adjustment of picked quantities is made without a system re-scan.

11. Picking accuracy is supported by inventory accuracy maintained under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts. Pickers do not post inventory adjustments. Where a pick face shows a stock discrepancy, picking from that face stops until a stock controller performs a recount and confirms availability or triggers replenishment.

12. Handheld WMS scanners are shared across shifts for picking, replenishment and packing verification. Scanners that fail to read or lose connection are removed from use and reported to the shift supervisor. Picking does not continue on paper without scan verification.

13. Roles are fixed for this section. Pickers own scanner-directed picking and scan verification. Forklift operators own replenishment moves. The shift supervisor in charge of the floor owns incident response for repeated mismatches on a face or order. The warehouse manager is accountable for the overall accuracy standard.

14. Safety rules apply to all picking, replenishment and packing work. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide, main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide, and pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide separated by yellow barriers. Speed limits are 10 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones and crossings.

title: Storage Capacity and Put-Away
text:
1. Bulk storage is provided in Zone B, the 2,200 m2 bulk storage area within the single-storey hall. Zone B contains high-bay pallet racking with 2,400 pallet positions and serves as the primary stockholding area for booked palletised goods.

2. Put-away to Zone B is limited to the available 2,400 pallet positions. Harborwick 3PL does not promise storage beyond the physical position count and weight limits of the racking. Allocation of positions to the Client is managed in the warehouse management system by the stock controllers.

3. Each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg. With a maximum of 1,000 kg per pallet, load included, this limit governs how many full-weight pallets may be placed in a single bay. No bay is loaded beyond its marked 2,700 kg limit under any circumstances.

4. Free block-stacking outside the racking is limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m stacking height. Block-stacked pallets also respect the 1,000 kg per pallet maximum. Stacking above 3 high or above 4.0 m is not permitted.

5. High-bay handling in Zone B is performed by reach trucks rated at 1.6 t and counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t. All equipment is electric. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide and rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide, and trucks operate within these widths under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.

6. Only booked goods are put away. Goods are booked in Zone A after document check, unloading, counting and inspection, and only inspected and system-booked quantities are released for put-away under PR-02 Put-away to storage. Unbooked, uninspected or undocumented goods remain in Zone A and are not moved to Zone B, E or F.

7. Put-away follows written procedure PR-02 and is executed with scanner-directed tasks. Every put-away move is scan-verified to the assigned Zone B location. Goods are not considered stored until the system confirms the location scan.

8. Chilled goods are not stored in Zone B. Products requiring +2 °C to +8 °C are put away only to Zone E, the 300 m2 cold zone with alarms and manual temperature verification each shift, under PR-12 Cold-chain handling. Ambient put-away tasks do not direct chilled product to Zone B racking.

9. Hazardous goods are not stored in Zone B. Goods requiring hazardous storage are put away only to the separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m2 in Zone F under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response. The cage holds at most 4,000 kg at a time, which is 4 full-weight pallets, and hazmat never sits anywhere else.

10. Zone C pick faces are not a storage area. Before each picking shift, pick faces in the 1,200 m2 picking zone are replenished from Zone B bulk under PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces. Replenishment is a separate scanner-directed move and does not change the Zone B capacity commitment.

11. Racking safety underpins the storage commitment. Racking receives a documented safety inspection every month by the maintenance technician, and damage found during put-away is reported to the shift supervisor immediately and quarantine action taken under PR-09 if stock is affected.

12. Roles are fixed for put-away and holding. Forklift operators execute put-away moves, stock controllers own location accuracy in the system, the shift supervisor runs the floor during each shift, and the warehouse manager is accountable for the site and final sign-offs.

13. Safety rules apply to all storage work. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Speed limits are 10 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h where people and trucks meet, and pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide separated by yellow barriers.

title: Counts, Adjustments and Reporting
text:
1. Inventory accuracy is maintained through continuous counting under written procedure PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts. The service standard is that the stock in the system is the stock on the rack, owned day to day by the stock controllers.

2. Cycle counts run every working day, Monday to Friday, on a rotating zone schedule covering Zone B bulk storage, Zone C pick faces, Zone E cold zone and Zone F holdings. Counting is performed by the stock controllers with scanner-directed tasks on handheld WMS scanners.

3. Counts are performed without interrupting committed inbound and outbound operations. Where a count requires a location to be frozen, the shift supervisor in charge of the floor approves the freeze and pickers and forklift operators work from alternate faces until the count is released.

4. Every count is a system-to-rack and rack-to-system check of product, quantity, location and condition. Chilled locations in Zone E and the hazmat cage in Zone F are counted in place under PR-12 Cold-chain handling and PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response, without breaking temperature control or cage segregation.

5. No inventory adjustment is ever posted on the basis of a single count. Any location showing a difference between system and physical stock is subject to a mandatory second count before any adjustment.

6. The second count is performed as a recount by a person independent of the first count, directed by the stock controllers and supervised by the shift supervisor. Put-away, replenishment and picking from that location stop until the recount is complete.

7. Only a confirmed recount difference becomes an adjustment proposal. Stock controllers prepare the proposal with first-count quantity, recount quantity, product and location evidence, and related inbound, picking or damage references where available.

8. Adjustments are posted only in the warehouse management system after approval and recount confirmation. Unconfirmed differences remain open and the location remains under review; goods are not moved to quarantine or written off on count evidence alone.

9. Once a year Harborwick 3PL shuts down for a full wall-to-wall stocktake of all zones. The stocktake covers every pallet position in the 2,400-position racking in Zone B, all pick faces in Zone C, the full Zone E cold zone, and all holdings in Zone F including quarantine, returns inspection and the hazmat cage.

10. The annual stocktake is directed by the stock controllers and run shift by shift under the shift supervisors. Every location is counted and every difference is recounted before adjustment, on the same recount-before-adjustment rule as daily cycle counts.

11. The warehouse manager personally signs off the stocktake results. No stocktake is closed and no final stocktake adjustments are reported to the Client without this sign-off. The signed result is the opening system stock for the next operating day.

12. Damaged-goods write-offs found through counts follow PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. The shift supervisor approves write-offs up to 500 EUR and the warehouse manager signs off any write-off above 500 EUR. Damaged units are moved to quarantine the same day they are found.

13. Reporting to the Client comprises a daily cycle-count summary with locations counted, matches found, recounts opened and adjustments posted, and a full annual stocktake report with opening, counted and adjusted quantities by product and location. Incident reports affecting stock accuracy are reviewed by the shift supervisor and made available on request.

14. End-of-shift handover under PR-15 applies to counting. Open recounts, frozen locations, unposted proposals and stocktake preparation tasks are recorded and handed to the next shift supervisor and stock controller team, so no count or adjustment is lost between shifts.

title: Responsibilities and Governance
text:
1. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site — operations, safety and final sign-offs. This accountability covers inventory accuracy, storage in Zones B, E and F, and all reports issued to the Client under Chapter 2.

2. Each shift is run by one shift supervisor in charge of the floor. The morning shift 06:00–14:00 and afternoon shift 14:00–22:00 each has a designated supervisor who directs floor staff, controls incident response, and ensures handover to the next shift under PR-15 End-of-shift handover.

3. The shift supervisor directs forklift operators, inbound operators, pickers, packing staff and floaters during the shift. No put-away, replenishment, picking or counting task proceeds against the supervisor's safety or freeze instruction.

4. The dispatcher owns dock scheduling. The dispatcher books transport, assigns every carrier a door and time slot, and releases outbound loads. Doors 1–4 are inbound only and Doors 5–8 are outbound only, and no door change is valid without dispatcher assignment.

5. Day-to-day inventory accuracy is owned by the 2 stock controllers. They direct the rotating daily cycle counts, order mandatory recounts, prepare adjustment proposals, and manage Zone B location allocation in the warehouse management system under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts.

6. Forklift operators execute scanner-directed put-away and replenishment moves only. They do not post adjustments, approve counts, or change locations. Pickers pick only against scanner tasks and stop from any face placed under count freeze or discrepancy review until released by a stock controller.

7. Inbound operators own unloading, counting and inspection in Zone A under PR-01 Inbound receiving. Only inspected and booked goods are released by them for put-away to Zone B, E or F under PR-02 Put-away to storage.

8. Returns and packing staff inspect returns in Zone F under PR-07 Returns handling and propose restock, rework or scrap. The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns. No return is restocked without that approval.

9. The maintenance technician maintains trucks, racking and dock equipment and logs every repair. The monthly racking safety inspection is performed and documented by the technician, and any rack damage affecting stored stock is escalated to the shift supervisor immediately.

10. Incident escalation runs from the floor to the shift supervisor to the warehouse manager. Every incident report is reviewed by the shift supervisor. Reports affecting stock accuracy, cold chain, hazmat segregation or rack safety are escalated to the warehouse manager the same shift.

11. Financial and closure sign-offs are fixed. The warehouse manager personally signs off the annual wall-to-wall stocktake results and any damaged-goods write-off above 500 EUR under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. The shift supervisor approves write-offs up to 500 EUR only.

12. Overtime, including Saturday morning peak-season working, is approved solely by the warehouse manager. Shift supervisors and dispatchers do not commit overtime or weekend counting or stocktake working without that approval.

13. Absence cover is provided by 2 floaters who work under the direction of the shift supervisor on duty. Use of floaters for counting, picking or put-away does not change ownership: stock controllers still own accuracy and the supervisor still owns the floor.

14. Governance is evidenced in writing. Shift handovers, dock assignments, count and recount records, adjustment approvals, incident reviews and manager sign-offs are retained and made available to the Client on request as the control trail for inventory control and reporting.

title: Damaged Goods and Quarantine
text:
1. Quarantine is the physically segregated holding area inside Zone F, the 600 m2 services and control zone. Only quarantined, damaged or suspect goods are held there pending inspection and disposition decision. Quarantine is separate from value-added packing, returns inspection and the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage.

2. Damaged-goods handling follows written procedure PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. This section defines the service commitment for identification, segregation, inspection and write-off approval. No damaged unit is restocked, reworked, scrapped or written off outside PR-09.

3. Any goods found damaged, leaking, crushed, wet, pest-affected, temperature-abused or otherwise suspect are moved to quarantine the same day they are found. This applies whether damage is found at receiving in Zone A, during put-away or replenishment, at pick faces in Zone C, during counts, or in Zone D staging.

4. Discovery is reported immediately to the shift supervisor in charge of the floor. The reporting operator secures the goods in place, prevents further handling damage, and arranges transfer to Zone F by forklift operator or pallet jack under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.

5. On transfer, the goods are labelled as quarantine hold with product, quantity, location of discovery, date, shift and reason. The stock controllers place the quantity on system hold so it cannot be allocated for picking, replenishment or dispatch. System hold is applied the same shift.

6. Quarantined goods are not stored in Zone B bulk storage, Zone C pick faces, Zone D dispatch or Zone E cold zone. Damaged chilled goods are held only in the quarantine provision that maintains +2 °C to +8 °C control, and damaged hazardous goods are held only under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response, never as general quarantine.

7. Every quarantine receipt is inspected in Zone F. Inspection is performed by stock controllers with inbound, returns or packing staff as directed by the shift supervisor, against delivery, put-away, pick and count references. Inspection records condition, photographs where needed, countable quantity and packaging state.

8. No adjustment or write-off is posted on inspection alone where quantity accuracy is in doubt. Where the system quantity differs, a mandatory second count under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts is completed before any adjustment proposal. Location freezes ordered for the recount are respected.

9. After inspection, a disposition is proposed: return to stock, rework and repack, hold for Client instruction, or scrap and write off. Returns and packing staff may propose restock, rework or scrap, and stock controllers propose inventory corrections. Only saleable, fully compliant units are ever proposed for return to stock.

10. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR. The warehouse manager signs off any damaged-goods write-off above 500 EUR, and no write-off above 500 EUR is posted or reported to the Client without that sign-off. Cumulative splitting to avoid the threshold is not permitted.

11. Restock from quarantine to Zone B, E or compliant Zone C locations is executed only after approval and only as a scanner-directed put-away under PR-02 Put-away to storage. Scrap is removed from system stock only after write-off approval, and physical disposal is recorded and logged.

12. Quarantine holdings are reviewed daily by the stock controllers and the shift supervisor. Goods are not left in quarantine without a disposition status, owner and next-review date. Overdue holds and holds awaiting Client instruction are listed in the daily cycle-count summary.

13. Every quarantine movement, inspection, disposition approval and write-off sign-off is retained as the control trail and made available to the Client on request. Incident reports affecting stock are reviewed by the shift supervisor and escalated to the warehouse manager the same shift.

14. Safety rules apply to all quarantine work. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory on the warehouse floor, speed limits are 10 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h where people and trucks meet, and pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide separated by yellow barriers. End-of-shift handover under PR-15 records open quarantine holds and pending approvals.

title: Returns Handling
text:
1. Returns are accepted within 14 days of delivery. Goods returned after 14 days are not accepted as returns and are held in Zone A pending Client instruction. The 14-day window is counted from the date of outbound delivery to the consignee.

2. All returns handling takes place in Zone F, the 600 m2 services and control zone. Returns inspection is performed in the designated returns inspection area, separate from quarantine, value-added packing and the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage. Returns handling follows written procedure PR-07 Returns handling.

3. Return arrivals use inbound Doors 1-4 only and require a prior time slot and door assignment from the dispatcher. The dispatcher owns dock scheduling. Drivers wait in the marked waiting area in the fenced yard and are not permitted in the hall or in Zone F working areas.

4. No return is unloaded before transport and return documents are checked. Document check is the mandatory first step under PR-01 Inbound receiving logic, and undeclared or undocumented goods are held in Zone A and are not moved to Zone F until documents are resolved.

5. Every returned unit is inspected in Zone F. Returns and packing staff inspect quantity, condition, packaging integrity, labelling, expiry and temperature history where applicable, against the original dispatch and Client return authorisation. No return is restocked, reworked or scrapped without complete inspection.

6. On receipt in Zone F, returned quantities are placed on system hold by the stock controllers. Held returns cannot be allocated for picking, replenishment or dispatch. System hold is applied the same shift as receipt.

7. Returned chilled goods are inspected without breaking +2 °C to +8 °C control and are held only in temperature-controlled provision under PR-12 Cold-chain handling. Returned hazardous goods are held only under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response in the hazmat cage, subject to the 4,000 kg limit. Hazmat never sits as general returns.

8. Units found damaged, leaking, crushed, wet, pest-affected or temperature-abused during returns inspection are moved to quarantine the same day they are found under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Quarantined returns are labelled as quarantine hold and excluded from restock until inspection and disposition are complete.

9. Where system quantity differs on a return, no adjustment is posted on inspection alone. A mandatory second count under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts is completed before any adjustment proposal, and the location remains frozen until the recount is confirmed.

10. After inspection, returns staff propose a disposition for each inspected quantity: restock to saleable stock, rework and repack, hold for Client instruction, or scrap. Only fully compliant, saleable units in intact packaging are ever proposed for restock.

11. The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns. No return is restocked, reworked or scrapped without that approval. Holds awaiting Client instruction are not disposed until written instruction is received.

12. Scrap and write-offs from returns follow PR-09 approval limits. The shift supervisor approves write-offs up to 500 EUR and the warehouse manager signs off any write-off above 500 EUR. Splitting to avoid the threshold is not permitted.

13. Approved restock is executed only as a scanner-directed put-away under PR-02 Put-away to storage to Zone B, Zone E or compliant Zone C locations. Approved scrap is removed from system stock only after write-off approval, with physical disposal recorded. Rework is performed in Zone F value-added packing and re-inspected before put-away.

14. Every returns receipt, inspection, recount, disposition approval and write-off sign-off is retained as the control trail and reported in the daily summary with overdue holds listed. Safety rules apply throughout: high-visibility vests and class S3 footwear are mandatory, speed limits are 10 km/h inside and 5 km/h where people and trucks meet. Open returns and pending approvals are handed over under PR-15 End-of-shift handover.

title: Chilled Storage Service
text:
1. Chilled storage is provided exclusively in Zone E, the 300 m2 cold zone within the single-storey hall. No other zone is a compliant chilled store. Ambient storage in Zone B, picking in Zone C, dispatch in Zone D, and general holdings in Zone F do not meet the chilled commitment.

2. Zone E is held between +2 °C and +8 °C at all times that chilled Client stock is present. This range applies to racked pallets, staged put-away, inspection work, counting work and any temperature-controlled quarantine provision for chilled goods.
