Stock outside this range is treated as temperature-abused.

3. Temperature control is continuous with audible and visual alarms on excursion or equipment fault. Alarms are responded to immediately by the shift supervisor in charge of the floor. Affected stock is placed on system hold by the stock controllers and is not picked, replenished or dispatched until checked.

4. A manual temperature verification is performed in Zone E during each shift, morning shift 06:00–14:00 and afternoon shift 14:00–22:00, including any Saturday morning overtime shift worked. The reading, time, location and verifier are recorded in writing. Missing verification is escalated to the shift supervisor the same shift.

5. Chilled handling follows written procedure PR-12 Cold-chain handling, supported by PR-01 Inbound receiving, PR-02 Put-away to storage, PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts and PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. No chilled receipt, move or release is made outside PR-12.

6. Only booked chilled goods are put away to Zone E. Goods are booked in Zone A after document check, unloading, counting and inspection, and chilled product identified at inspection is directed only to Zone E under scanner-directed PR-02 tasks. Chilled goods are never put away to Zone B racking or general Zone F holdings.

7. Time outside temperature control is minimised. Chilled pallets are moved directly between Zone A inspection, Zone E, compliant chilled pick locations and Zone D loading, by forklift operators using electric equipment under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Doors to Zone E are kept closed except for active moves, and chilled goods are not left waiting in Zone A, C or D.

8. Replenishment of chilled pick faces is made only from Zone E and only to designated compliant chilled locations, before each picking shift under PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces. Pickers pick chilled orders only against scanner tasks and every item is scan-verified before packing, under PR-04 Order picking and PR-05 Packing and labelling.

9. Chilled dispatch staging in Zone D is limited to wrapped, labelled pallets staged for the assigned outbound door under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Staging time is kept to the assigned slot, and no chilled load is loaded without dispatcher release. After release the truck is loaded and sealed without delay.

10. Cycle counts of Zone E are performed in place every working day on the rotating schedule, without breaking +2 °C to +8 °C control. No adjustment is posted on a single count. Any difference triggers a mandatory second count, with the location frozen by the shift supervisor until the recount is confirmed.

11. Chilled units found damaged, leaking, pest-affected, wet, crushed or temperature-abused are moved to quarantine the same day they are found, to the quarantine provision that maintains +2 °C to +8 °C control. General quarantine without temperature control is not used for chilled goods. Disposition and write-off follow PR-09, with supervisor approval up to 500 EUR and warehouse manager sign-off above 500 EUR.

12. Returned chilled goods are inspected in Zone F without breaking cold-chain control and held only in temperature-controlled provision under PR-12 and PR-07 Returns handling. Every unit is inspected, held on system hold the same shift, and restocked only after shift-supervisor approval of final disposition and only as scanner-directed put-away to Zone E or a compliant location.

13. Roles are fixed. The warehouse manager is accountable for cold-chain integrity and final sign-offs. The shift supervisor runs incident response for alarms, excursions and verification failures. Stock controllers own system hold, counts and recounts. The maintenance technician maintains refrigeration and alarms and logs every repair. The annual wall-to-wall stocktake includes the full Zone E and is signed off by the warehouse manager.

14. Every alarm, verification reading, excursion, hold, inspection and approval is retained as the control trail and reported in the daily summary, with overdue holds listed. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory, speed limits are 10 km/h inside and 5 km/h where people and trucks meet. Open chilled holds, alarms and pending decisions are handed over under PR-15 End-of-shift handover.
